    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1471 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Liveandletsfly ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Airline Captain Defends 20-Year-Old Female Copilot After Fatal Learjet Crash

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1471 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Liveandletsfly

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • 121pilot, our resident commercial airline pilot on Live And Let’s Fly, examines what we know about the crash of Learjet 60 N722BD and pushes back against the rush to blame its young first officer, Nathalia Filgueiras.
    • The crash of N722BD, a Learjet 60 operating on a charter flight, has drawn enormous attention.
    • In a recent development, as is typical of the aviation YouTube community, many of whom I respect, people have been rushing to get videos out about this accident.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    121pilot, our resident commercial airline pilot on Live And Let’s Fly, examines what we know about the crash of Learjet 60 N722BD and pushes back against the rush to blame its young first officer, Nathalia Filgueiras.

    The crash of N722BD, a Learjet 60 operating on a charter flight, has drawn enormous attention. Much of that is understandable. We have extremely dramatic video of the aircraft descending almost vertically at a very high rate of speed, along with equally dramatic ATC audio recordings.

    In a recent development, as is typical of the aviation YouTube community, many of whom I respect, people have been rushing to get videos out about this accident. What I really don’t care for, however, are the clickbait titles. Titles like “Could Any Pilot Have Saved This Learjet 60?” or “Lear 60 Florida Crash: It Happened Before” or “Expert Pilot Explains What Likely Caused SHOCKING Plane Crash in Florida” by Megyn Kelly.

    These kinds of titles make me angry because, regardless of the actual content of the videos, they are misleading. The simple fact is that we know very little about this accident at this point, and certainly not enough to be speculating about a probable cause.

    In a recent development, the aircraft, a Learjet Model 60 with nine people aboard, reported moderate turbulence and icing at Flight Level 350 and requested a climb to Flight Level 370. Moments later, the aircraft departed controlled flight, eventually entering a descent at an extraordinarily high rate of speed.

    We know that the NTSB has recovered components of the horizontal stabilizer that separated from the aircraft, and widely circulated video appears to show the aircraft without this crucial component.

    In a recent development, what we DON’T know is whether the aircraft flew into a thunderstorm. The weather imagery I’ve seen to date comes from sources that have time lags built into them and don’t necessarily represent the real-time weather picture. We don’t know what caused the horizontal stabilizer to separate, or even when that happened. Did it separate during the dive, or was its failure what initiated the dive? That’s an key distinction, and right now it’s an unknown.

    Industry observers note that we know the Learjet 60’s wing is sensitive to ice accumulation and that the aircraft is susceptible to a phenomenon called Mach tuck. We don’t know whether either played any role in this accident, or even whether the aircraft’s critical surfaces had accumulated ice.

    Industry observers note that we know the aircraft had been operating at higher altitudes, with a reported descent from Flight Level 410 to 350 before the final sequence of events. But without knowing the aircraft’s speed, configuration, weight, and other performance parameters, we cannot draw meaningful conclusions about its operating margins.

    We know the captain was 55 years old and very experienced. We know the first officer was 20 years old and relatively inexperienced, but fully qualified to act as a second in command.

    Recent findings suggest that we know the CVR, or cockpit voice recorder, has been recovered, but we don’t yet know whether its contents can be successfully recovered or what information it might provide. We also know the aircraft was not equipped with a flight data recorder, or FDR. That means information about the aircraft’s speed, heading, pitch, roll, system status, and other parameters may remain unknown or will have to be reconstructed using external data sources and whatever information can be gleaned from the CVR.

    But perhaps the most disturbing part of this entire event, aside from the tragic loss of life, has been the reaction of so many people who couldn’t explain the difference between a slat and a flap, yet have felt perfectly qualified to judge the performance of the first officer based on her age and gender.

    In the Megyn Kelly video, she questions whether someone who isn’t even old enough to drink should have been acting as a pilot.

    I think the better question is why we allow 18-year-olds to join the military and go into combat, but apparently don’t think they’re old enough to have a beer. Why can a 20-year-old warrant officer fly a Black Hawk full of troops into the maelstrom of a hot landing zone, but we think he or she can’t be trusted with alcohol?

    Even more disgusting have been some of the reactions to the ATC recordings.

    It has been revealed that first, let me suggest that if you haven’t already listened to them, don’t. Second, and most importantly, as a 56-year-old male airline captain, I hear absolutely nothing in that recording, either in her voice or in her actions, that merits criticism.

    I don’t think people who haven’t experienced it can appreciate just how incredibly violent and terrifying that initial descent must have been. In one recording, we go from a seemingly calm situation, with the crew requesting a climb, to a loss of control and a reported descent of approximately 8,000 feet per minute in about 10 seconds. Just 16 seconds later, the aircraft is in an overspeed condition, and the first officer reports a descent rate of 20,000 feet per minute. That’s an absolutely eye-watering number. It defies belief and would be utterly terrifying to any pilot. About 10 seconds later, she reports that they are going to crash into the ground. Not long after that, someone can be heard in the background reciting the Lord’s Prayer.

    I don’t know this for certain, of course, but my suspicion is that somewhere during this sequence the crew became aware that the horizontal stabilizer had separated and that they had lost the ability to recover the aircraft.

    If there is anything to be remarked about her performance as a pilot, it’s that she was clearly doing her job right up to the end.

    We teach Aviate, Navigate, Communicate. Aviate means flying the airplane. Navigate means determining where you need to go and how to get there. Communicate means keeping the appropriate people informed.

    In this situation, the captain was presumably concentrating on flying the aircraft while the first officer was communicating with ATC. That is exactly what we expect from a two-person crew in an emergency, assuming those were their respective roles at the time.

    In a recent development, what’s more, in the absence of an FDR, the information she provided to ATC may prove absolutely crucial to understanding what happened. We may eventually discover that her actions and communications were instrumental in allowing the NTSB to piece together this accident. That information could well save lives in the future.

    I also find it interesting, and troubling, that contrary to the media’s usual fixation on the captain, as though he’s flying the airplane solo, the exact opposite has happened here. The first officer has become the focus of an extraordinary amount of attention, even though we have not established who was flying the aircraft.

    Sources indicate that it’s been my absolute privilege to fly with a number of female pilots throughout my career, and not one of them has ever done anything less than a sterling job. Frankly, the airplane doesn’t care about your gender or the color of your skin. And when it comes to aviation, that’s exactly how it should be. We should care about qualifications and competence. That’s it.

    If I step onto my jet tomorrow and find a young female first officer waiting for me, I’ll be just as happy to have her there as I would a young male. At this point in my career, flying with a young and relatively inexperienced first officer gives me the opportunity to act as a mentor and pass along some hard-won flying wisdom. That’s something I genuinely enjoy. Nathalia had earned her place in that cockpit. Not one iota of the solid evidence we have right now leads me to believe that this accident can or should be blamed on her.

    It may well turn out that crew errors figure prominently in the probable cause. We simply don’t know yet. But if that turns out to be the case, it’s notable to remember that the captain was the pilot in command. He was responsible for the operation of that aircraft, and the first officer was serving under his command. If poor decision-making put the aircraft into a situation from which there was no escape, the captain would bear the primary responsibility for those decisions.

    Industry observers note that but that’s a hypothetical. And right now, we don’t know that any such decisions were made.

    We owe the nine people who lost their lives, their families, and the people who will eventually investigate this accident something better than speculation, sensationalism, and a rush to judgment.

    Industry observers note that ANALYSIS -- “Life moves pretty fast,” that famed 20th-century philosopher Ferris Bueller once noted. “If you don't stop and look around once in a while, you could miss it.”.

    In 2024, Democrats were consigned to the political wilderness. Republicans had captured the White House, flipped the Senate and held the House. President Donald Trump had completely altered the party coalitions as he led the ascendant GOP to victory.

    Now, just two years later, Democrats are on the rise. A historic midterm tsunami has swept them into such commanding Senate and House majorities that some are questioning whether Republicans will ever be in charge again. And if Texas is blue, how does the GOP have any chance in the Electoral College again?

    A big takeaway from the midterm results should be that there’s very little permanence in our politics.

    What may have looked like a newly introduced GOP coalition was really more of a Trump coalition, and it crumbled in the face of economic frustrations, affordability concerns and the president’s unpopular policies.

    With Trump’s negative job approval rating weighing them down, Republican candidates suffered losses among virtually all demographic groups – including by wide margins among constituencies thought to make up the GOP’s core.

    Trump or the Republicans finished ahead among male voters by 4 points in 2018, 8 points in 2020, 14 points in 2022 and 12 points in 2024, according to the exit polls. Men went for Democratic candidates by 4 points (51 percent to 47 percent) this cycle. Meanwhile, Republicans lost even more ground among women. While Kamala Harris finished ahead of Trump by 8 points in 2024, that margin grew to 21 points for Democratic candidates this year.

    Trump closed the gap among Hispanic voters to just 5 points behind Harris two years ago. This year, Hispanic voters nationwide supported Democratic candidates by 32 points (65 percent to 33 percent). Even white voters shifted significantly. They backed Trump or  Republican candidates by 10 points in 2018, 17 points in 2020, 18 points in 2022 and 15 points in 2024. And yet Democrats edged out Republicans by a point (50 percent to 49 percent) on Nov. 3.

    According to recent reports, voters without a college degree were supposed to be a key cog in Republicans’ latest populist coalition. But they went from +13 (56 percent to 43 percent) for Trump in 2024 to backing Republican candidates by just 1 point this year. Meanwhile, the gap among voters with a college degree went from 14 points for Harris in 2024 to 30 points for Democrats this cycle.

    Industry observers note that republicans had closed the gap among young voters aged 18 to 29 from 35 points in 2018 to just 11 points in 2024. But younger voters supported Democratic candidates this year by 50 points (74 percent to 24 percent). Not to mention Democrats flipped voters aged 45 to 64 for the first time in nearly two decades.

    It has been revealed that white evangelicals appear to be one of the only groups that didn’t shift toward Democrats. They supported GOP candidates 82 percent to 17 percent. But they only made up 17 percent of the electorate, according to the exit polls, which is down from a very consistent 25 percent for more than a decade. So there was still a problem with that group of voters, but it was more about turnout than persuasion.

    Recent findings suggest that while there was an unmistakable leftward shift this year, the results should not be considered a permanent party realignment any more than 2024 was. While Democrats did extremely well in Texas this year, they still haven’t won the Lone Star State in a presidential race in 50 years. So maybe it’s wise for everyone to take a deep breath.

    Recent findings suggest that if you take this year’s election results and match them with the Senate seats on the ballot in 2028, there doesn’t appear to be a viable path for Republicans back to the majority. But there wasn’t a particularly viable Democratic path to the Senate majority at this point two years ago. And if the Alaska election goes their way, they will end up winning Senate races in seven states that were initially rated Solid Republican.

    If one party starts to get too comfortable, voters have a way of bringing politicians back down to earth. If Democrats come to Congress and push too far to the left or become too defined by their most extreme members, they will squander the opportunity they earned this year.

    The dramatic demographic swings should be evidence that many voters are not beholden to either party and are open to switching allegiances, particularly in a time of economic uncertainty.

    At the same time, if Republicans don’t go through some time of reflection and instead triple down on the policies that led to the blue wave, they risk cementing some of the shifts that started this cycle. It just won’t be thick cement.

    • Recent findings suggest that have an idea for a livery that we should highlight?
    • Industry observers note that iberia’s standard livery combines a predominantly white fuselage with a red-and-yellow tail inspired by the colors of Spain’s national flag.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, editor’s Note: AirlineGeeks is proud to present our ‘Livery of the Week’ series. Every Friday, a team member will share an airline livery, which can be from the past, present, or even a special scheme. Some airline liveries are works of art. The complexity associated with painting around critical flight components and the added weight requires outside-the-box thinking from designers. The average airliner can cost upwards of $200,000 to repaint, creating a separate aircraft repainting industry as a result.

    Recent findings suggest that have an idea for a livery that we should highlight? Drop us a line.

    Industry observers note that iberia’s standard livery combines a predominantly white fuselage with a red-and-yellow tail inspired by the colors of Spain’s national flag. Introduced in 2013, the design marked the carrier’s first major rebranding in more than three decades.

    The airline unveiled its newly introduced corporate identity on October 15, 2013, as part of a broader restructuring effort. The redesign replaced the familiar red, orange, and yellow stripes that had appeared on Iberia aircraft since the late 1970s.

    The most prominent change came on the vertical stabilizer. Iberia introduced a sweeping red-and-yellow design that extends from the tail onto the rear fuselage. A white diagonal section separates the two colors, giving the aircraft a different appearance from the geometric logo used on the previous livery.

    Sources indicate that the fuselage also received a substantial upgrade. Large red “IBERIA” titles replaced the smaller lettering used on earlier aircraft, while the horizontal stripes running along the windows were eliminated. The result was a predominantly white aircraft with most of its color concentrated toward the tail.

    Iberia’s latest branding retained the red and yellow of the Spanish flag but removed the royal crown from its main corporate logo. The crown had been part of the airline’s previous identity and remained represented separately on aircraft near their registration markings.

    The redesign followed Iberia’s 2011 merger with British Airways under International Airlines Group. At the time, the Spanish carrier was undergoing a significant restructuring that included changes to its fleet, route network, and passenger experience.

    The first aircraft to receive the updated livery was an Airbus A330-300 named *Juan Carlos I*, which was presented in November 2013. The new appearance was subsequently introduced across the airline’s fleet as aircraft underwent scheduled repainting.

    Sources indicate that iberia’s earlier livery had been introduced in 1977 and featured a stylized red-and-yellow “IB” logo on the tail. Although the design received minor updates over the years, its basic appearance remained recognizable on aircraft ranging from Boeing 727s and 747s to Airbus A320s and A340s.

    The current scheme has since appeared on several generations of Iberia aircraft, including Airbus A320-family jets, A330s and A350s. It also appears on the airline’s Airbus A321XLR fleet, which entered service in 2024 as Iberia became the launch operator of the long-range narrowbody.

    Sources indicate that iberia has occasionally introduced special liveries celebrating milestones in its history, including retro designs commemorating the airline’s earlier aircraft. Its standard scheme, however, has remained largely unchanged since the 2013 rebranding.

    The Best Hotels Near Disneyland Paris With Cinderella Suites, 'Toy Story'–Themed Rooms, and Quaint Cottages

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Located just 40 minutes from Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport, Disneyland Paris is the ideal place to begin a Parisian vacation or say au revoir before returning home.
    • There's also never been a better time to visit.
    • Sources indicate that of course, you'll need somewhere to rest your head at night, and that's where the best hotels near Disneyland Paris come into play.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Located just 40 minutes from Paris Charles de Gaulle Airport, Disneyland Paris is the ideal place to begin a Parisian vacation or say au revoir before returning home. Disneyland Paris's two theme parks, Disneyland Park and Disney Adventure World, pair timeless charm with an ease you'll never find stateside. Here, you can sip Champagne in front of Sleeping Beauty's castle—or visit a dragon beneath it—while filling your days with delightful architecture, unprecedented thrills, and the wildest wilderness ride Disney's ever built (Massive Thunder Mountain!).

    There's also never been a better time to visit. Walt Disney Studios Park's March 2026 transformation into the new Disney Adventure World brought a drone-filled nighttime show, Avengers coaster, and even a Frozen-themed land featuring a lifelike Olaf robot to its once-faltering second gate. Now, between Fantasyland classics and futuristic favorites, there's something new and thrilling for the entire family to experience.

    Sources indicate that of course, you'll need somewhere to rest your head at night, and that's where the best hotels near Disneyland Paris come into play. Staying at a Disney-branded property typically affords guests special amenities including ticket packages, exclusive character meet-and-greets, and Extra Magic Time, which provides bonus time in the parks prior to opening. These hotels are great options, but can also be pricey—luckily, there are also a few non-branded properties in the area that make for great alternatives. There's something here for everyone and every budget.

    Unsure of whether you want to add something so Américain to your Paris vacation? As a theme park journalist who has visited all Disney parks worldwide, trust me: It's worth the visit. Even with so many cultural monuments in Paris, nothing is more delightfully uncanny than witnessing the United States section of It's a Small World. So, whether you're looking for glamour or simply a good location, read on for the very best hotels near Disneyland Paris.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: Three-minute walk.

    As the crown jewel of France's Disney resort, this 487-room property is Disney's best hotel overseas—and, quite possibly, in the entire world. After undergoing an extensive three-year overhaul, the iconic pink palace reopened in 2024 with princess suites and luxurious amenities worthy of its five-star ranking. Great for couples or families, guests can anticipate the ultimate royal treatment thanks to rooms with romantic castle views just steps from the park. With kids treatments at the Spa by Clarins and two complimentary hours of childcare each day, parents can unwind at the Fleur de Lys bar, enjoy a prix fixe meal at chef Jean Imbert's on-site restaurant, or perhaps even sneak back into the parks themselves. (We won't tell.).

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: Eight-minute drive.

    It has been revealed that rustic-chic in the best of ways, Marriott's Village d'Île-de-France offers cozy abodes that sleep up to eight with full kitchens, washing machines, and plenty of space to stretch out, all a short shuttle ride from the theme parks. Designed to emulate the charms of a small Parisian village, these quaint studios and multi-bedroom town houses feel more like cottages than traditional vacation rentals. Surroundings like these may sound quotidien to someone like Princess Belle, but the resort is as sweet as the rooms are spacious, making it an ideal choice for a hotel near Disneyland Paris as well as extended trips to nearby towns.

    Check Availability at Booking.com.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: 10-minute walk, 10-minute drive.

    According to recent reports, considering it's the only hotel in the world dedicated to Marvel's famed comic book characters, it's no surprise the Infinity Stone–colored beverages and slick, silver rooms at Disney Hotel New York - The Art of Marvel are somewhat out of this world. Family-friendly amenities like superhero meet-and-greets and a design studio with character drawing experiences make it the ultimate getaway for any comic book–obsessed fan in your family. Yet, even with hundreds of unique pieces of artwork, it won't feel like you're living through an Infinity War. Delicately executed details, like Manhattan Restaurant's Asgard-inspired chandelier and Spider-Man swinging across the panel screens at Skyline Bar, provide simple city elegance with the lightest touch of Marvel magic.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: 17-minute walk, 8-minute drive.

    Sources indicate that if this hotel reminds you of Walt Disney World's Yacht & Beach Club resorts, you're not mistaken—this 1,098-room Disneyland Paris hotel was inspired by its Florida counterpart. The nautical theming is strong, and it's that seaside charm that keeps parkgoers returning to this waterfront escape. Just a 15-minute walk from the park gates, guests can meet maritime Mickey & Minnie Mouse (who don delightful cruisewear) or indulge in a seafood buffet at the aptly named Cape Cod restaurant. It's modeled after a familiar location back in the States, sure, but after spending the day with princesses, dragons, and superheroes, you may find yourself overjoyed to return to those country club comforts.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: 13-minute walk, 8-minute drive.

    Craving a bit more theming on your Disneyland Paris trip? Look no further than this national park–inspired escape. It offers lodge-style living perfect for a wintertime trip. Cozy up to the Redwood Bar & Lounge hearth, or in one of the newly renovated rooms with nods to Bambi and Pocahontas, and take in the charms of what Disney does best. Multiple on-site buffets allow you to feast like you've been on the move all day because, well, you likely have.

    Industry observers note that note that this Disney-operated hotel is right now undergoing a phased refurbishment. For stays in late 2026 and early 2027, I recommend selecting a refurbished room in The Lodges. Starting in February 2027, construction will move to general hotel spaces, and certain facilities will be temporarily unavailable.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: 30-minute walk, 10-minute drive.

    In a recent development, rooms at the boutique Hôtel l’Elysée Val d’Europe are modern and minimal, offering the perfect escape from any theme park chaos. Though it's just a 30-minute walk or a short, free shuttle ride away from the gates, the real perk of being a bit removed is its proximity to the Val d’Europe shopping complex and the designer outlet mall La Vallée Village. With a bounty of discounted prices on luxury brands like Prada, Saint Laurent, and Gucci, you're sure to find a Parisian souvenir that'll rival the array of Mickey Mouse goods sold within the parks.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: Nine-minute drive.

    Recent findings suggest that if the City of Lights appeals to you for its style and romance, consider this your ideal hotel. Design-forward rooms with concrete walls, sleek bathrooms, and an open, plant-walled lobby offer reliable value without sacrificing taste, making it a perfect choice for travelers seeking something a little less Disney. While families will benefit from select rooms offering full kitchens and stovetops, the upgraded amenities—which include a heated indoor pool, sauna, and hammam—offer a little something for everyone, just beyond the parks.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: 16-minute walk, 10-minute drive.

    Step right up to this quirky hotel that feels like a Western film set and is jam-packed with Toy Story details. Small touches, like cowprint bedspreads and appearances by Woody and Jessie, make Disney Hotel Cheyenne a hidden gem that's nearly as themed as Disneyland Paris's own Frontierland. Given that it's significantly more affordable than the majority of its Disneyland-owned counterparts yet retains perks like Extra Magic Time, this property offers a best-of-both-worlds approach for those who want to live a full Disney-fied day from first rides to fireworks.

    Distance from Disneyland Paris: 10-minute drive.

    Multi-room cabins at this expansive, woodsy resort are the perfect way to experience a taste of the outdoors between trips on Major Thunder Mountain. Sadly, there are no theme park shuttle services, so parks must be reached by car, rideshare, or taxi. But that's not to say it's worth skipping—here, nature abounds in both form and function. There's an on-site aviary, comfort food at the Crockett's Tavern buffet, and plenty of rustic charm, so the comforts of home are never too far away. Consider this Disneyland Paris hotel as close as you can get to camping at Disneyland's theme parks—if camping also included unfettered access to Mickey waffles.

    What area is the best to stay in when visiting Disneyland Paris?

    According to recent reports, any hotel near Disney Village, the entertainment and dining district at the entrance to Disneyland Paris's two theme parks, is going to be the most convenient choice. This not only offers more ease and access, but affords you the option to shop and dine after the parks close each night. Still, booking nearly any Disney-operated hotel will give you benefits like Extra Magic Time and exclusive character encounters, which help get you even more out of your Disneyland Paris vacation.

    Are there any hotels that are walking distance to Disneyland Paris?

    Yes—but you might want to bring your sneakers. Disneyland Hotel is located directly at the entrance to Disneyland Paris, while Disney Hotel New York - The Art of Marvel, Disney Newport Bay Club, and Disney Sequoia Lodge are all a 10- to 15-minute walk through Disney Village to reach both parks. Disney Hotel Cheyenne is a further trek, about 15 to 20 minutes away, but absolutely doable. Shuttle buses are available as well.

    What is the 3-2-1 rule at Disneyland Paris?

    Recent findings suggest that the 3-2-1 rule is essentially shorthand for how to streamline your Disneyland Paris experience. Experts recommend selecting three rides, two entertainment offerings, and one dining option for an easy, straightforward approach to planning a day at any Disney theme park. It works as well at Walt Disney World and Disneyland as it does here at Disneyland Paris, but I recommend you still do a little research before you go. Be sure you don't skip Phantom Manor, which can only be found in Paris, secure your dining reservations early, and don't miss the nighttime shows offered at both parks—they're among the best in the world.

    It is best to stay within the park at Disneyland Paris, or outside of it?

    It goes without saying that the closer you are to the castle, the “better” your hotel will be, but it shouldn't be a deal-breaker. Convenience is always a factor, but Disney-operated hotels at Disneyland Paris tend to be much pricier than their American counterparts, so staying a bus ride away might be necessary. Still, the perks are plenty across most of Disneyland's own hotels, including extra time in the parks, which is why I recommended so many of them.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    A flight attendant signing with a young passenger is a lovely moment on its own. But seeing five-year-old Luca meet American Airlines CEO Robert Isom, who learned a few signs to greet him, made me smile even more. We spend plenty of time examining what airlines get wrong. Here is something American got right.

    Luca is five years old, Deaf, and loves airplanes. In a video shared by American Airlines, a flight attendant communicates with him in sign language near the aircraft door and. again onboard. Watching Luca respond is delightful.

    In a recent development, there is something particularly sweet about seeing a child discover that someone outside his family can communicate with him in his own language. The flight attendant takes the time to engage with Luca directly, and his reaction is precious.

    The family later shared footage of a visit to American Airlines in Dallas, including a meeting with Isom.

    Recent findings suggest that according to his mother, Isom took the time to learn how to spell his name and sign “nice to meet you” in American Sign Language. He also gave Luca American Airlines trading cards, which she said he was very excited about.

    Her explanation of why the meeting mattered was simple:.

    “I can’t tell you how much it means when someone takes that extra step to communicate with him.”.

    A post shared by CALLIE FOSTER (@thelacouple).

    According to recent reports, in another post about the visit, she described hundreds of American employees gathering to welcome Luca, with many having learned some sign language for him. She remarked the family had not known what American had planned and was overwhelmed by the reception.

    That is quite a day for a little boy who loves airplanes.

    These small gestures make a huge difference…isn’t that true of so many things in life?

    Isom could have posed for a photograph, handed over the trading cards, and still called it a successful visit. Instead, he learned enough to introduce himself and greet Luca directly. Taking a little time beforehand allowed him to participate in the conversation rather than leave all the communicating to Luca’s parents.

    Recent findings suggest that the same goes for the employees who learned signs before welcoming him. It is easy to talk about the need to “care for people on life’s journey” (the current AA slogan). Here, they did something practical to make that happen.

    As a father, I understand why his mother was so touched. When someone makes an effort for your child, you remember it. A brief interaction that an employee might regard as a small part of the workday can become something a family talks about long afterward.

    In a recent development, and yes, American shared the encounter on social media. I am glad it did. There is room to recognize good hospitality even when an airline benefits from showing it.

    Between the flight attendant signing with Luca and the welcome he received at American’s campus, this family has some wonderful memories to take home. I appreciated watching Isom make the effort too. Learning a greeting is a modest undertaking, but his mother’s account explains how much it meant. Well done to everyone at American who helped make Luca feel so welcome. This was a refreshing bit of airline news to watch.

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: Beginner’s luck: Freshmen leave it to chance at House office lottery

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (925 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, rep.-elect Mark Teixeira reacts after drawing the worst chip during Tuesday’s lottery for newly elected members of Congress.
    • As far as birthdays go, Rep.-elect Shannon Taylor was having a pretty good one.
    • Crowded into a room in the Capitol Visitor Center on Tuesday morning with the rest of her freshman class, the Virginia Democrat walked up to a table with a wooden box and reached in.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, rep.-elect Mark Teixeira reacts after drawing the worst chip during Tuesday’s lottery for newly elected members of Congress. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    As far as birthdays go, Rep.-elect Shannon Taylor was having a pretty good one.

    Crowded into a room in the Capitol Visitor Center on Tuesday morning with the rest of her freshman class, the Virginia Democrat walked up to a table with a wooden box and reached in.

    “This is so nervewracking,” she said, before pulling out a chip with a “1” printed on it.

    According to recent reports, her prize was a coveted one — first choice of office space. Every two years, incoming members of the House play a game of chance to see who can land the best real estate and who will be relegated to less desirable corners of the Capitol complex.

    Sources indicate that the room broke out in raucous applause and a standing ovation. Her new colleagues started singing “Happy Birthday.”.

    Not everyone was so lucky. Rep.-elect Mark Teixeira, R-Texas, pulled number 105 — the very last one. The former MLB player raised his arms in a mock celebration.

    “Lets all hope for the luck of the Taylors,” stated Rep.-elect Brent Taylor, R-Tenn., only to emerge with number 81.

    The newly-elected members got their turn in a random order, walking up one by one to a table where deputy executive director of House Office Buildings Kornell Rancy kept watch over the box of chips.

    It has been revealed that rep.-elect John Cowan, R-Ga., was the first to pick a number. The first neurosurgeon to be elected to Congress, Cowan wore his white doctor’s coat as he pulled number 11 out of the box.

    “I wanted to do something where I’m just representing health care providers around the country,” Cowan stated.

    In a recent development, as returning members lay claim to more desirable offices made available by those who resign, retire or lose elections, the space they’ve abandoned is left for the newcomers, who are on the Hill this week for orientation. Many of them will end up in the Longworth Building, where suites can be awkward or cramped.

    Not all offices are created equal, and the calculus has changed over the years. The previously undesirable Cannon Building just underwent a budget-busting renovation that lasted more than a decade, with a spacious courtyard opening earlier this year. But the coveted Rayburn Building still retains its prestige, despite repeated and dire warnings from the Architect of the Capitol about its crumbling infrastructure.

    “You’re welcome,” stated Rep.-elect Amish Shah, D-Ariz., after pulling a disappointing number 94.

    Prior to the lottery, Rep.-elect Trever Nehls, R-Texas, was hoping for the best but had a backup plan in case his number noted otherwise.

    Recent findings suggest that “If I don’t pick number one, I’m going to offer one of these cigars as a trade to whoever gets it,” he remarked, pointing to three of them sticking out of his jacket pocket. He’s preparing to take over the seat at the moment held by his twin brother Troy, who shares a fondness for stogies.

    The office space lottery dates back to 1908, when members of the 60th Congress received their first office assignments after the completion of what would be named the Cannon Building. A House page drew names and numbers from a box, and members selected their offices from a chart, according to House Office Buildings executive director of facility operations Joe Yates, who kicked things off Tuesday with a history lesson.

    The lottery now is a little more modern, with members poring over virtual office layouts and doing walkthroughs of spaces on laptops.

    Recent findings suggest that “If somebody had to get 105, I’m glad it was me because I am here to serve, and I’m serving my freshman class by picking the worst office,” Teixeira remarked. “This is low on my priority list.”.

    Some members announced their lucky draws themselves, while others let Yates break the news.

    “Come visit me,” stated Rep.-elect Chris Gober, R-Texas, after pulling number 2 from the box.

    After the lottery itself, members huddled with their staff to strategize about the next steps — how to leverage their numbers and select the best suites left on the list, while also exploring layouts, paint colors and carpeting.

    “First and foremost, a good layout, so we can do good work, and people can be comfortable in doing the work, and then a convenient location. Very utilitarian,” remarked Rep.-elect Scott Wiener, D-Calif., of his priorities.

    It has been revealed that “We’ll get a decent Longworth office,” said Wiener, who drew pick 43. “Cannon would have been ideal, but I’m happy with any office.”.

    Recent findings suggest that rep.-elect Manny Rutinel, D-Colo., was hoping to replicate the good luck of some of his colleagues. “I’m going to do the Shannon Taylor and Sam Forstag. It’s eyes closed, behind the back,” he stated of his moves, reaching into the box. But it wasn’t enough, and Rutinel pulled number 69.

    Recent findings suggest that “These are not red numbers, these are not blue numbers. These are the remaining numbers, and there ain’t that many,” said Rep.-elect Johnny Garcia, D-Texas, who was among the last few people to pick. He emerged with number 75.

    And when Rep.-elect Joe Strada, R-Fla., the last of the incoming members to draw, walked up to the table, the whole room cheered.

    “Wouldn’t it be crazy if I picked number 1?” he joked, pulling out the last chip in the box.

    #77227. A Guide to NYC’s Little Italy—and the Culinary Gems Hidden Among the Tourist Traps

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1409 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cntraveler ↗ Open Full Page

    A Guide to NYC’s Little Italy—and the Culinary Gems Hidden Among the Tourist Traps

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1409 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Contrary to other tourist-focused neighborhoods in New York (looking at you, Times Square), Little Italy boasts an innate charm that resonates with visitors and locals alike.
    • A note on how we’re defining the area: Over the years, Little Italy’s boundaries have shrunk to focus on the touristic area of Mulberry Street and its immediate surroundings.
    • Sources indicate that located in the heart of Little Italy, Umberto’s Clam House is best known for its—you guessed it, all things clams.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Contrary to other tourist-focused neighborhoods in New York (looking at you, Times Square), Little Italy boasts an innate charm that resonates with visitors and locals alike. Sandwiched between SoHo and the Lower East Side, this jewel box area is home to long-standing, family-owned restaurants and authentic Italian bakeries, the majority of which have been neighborhood staples for decades. Yet despite its touristy atmosphere, a unique feeling of old school New York magic hangs in the air; beyond the personality-less stands and souvenir shops, framed family photos on restaurant walls and structural imperfections of tenement buildings speak to a bygone area of the city’s past, evoking a sense of nostalgia that so many neighborhoods lack. Pop down to Mulberry Street and see for yourself—though be sure you know which spots are actually legit (that’s where we come in).

    A note on how we’re defining the area: Over the years, Little Italy’s boundaries have shrunk to focus on the touristic area of Mulberry Street and its immediate surroundings. While the southern and western boundaries of Canal Street and Lafayette Streets remain unchanged, the historic easterly Bowery boundary has arguably shifted to Elizabeth Street; similarly, the northerly boundary of Kenmare has also condensed down, according to many, to Broome Street. For the sake of this piece, we’re using the boundaries of Lafayette Street, Canal Street, Elizabeth Street, and Broome Street as a happy medium.

    Sources indicate that located in the heart of Little Italy, Umberto’s Clam House is best known for its—you guessed it, all things clams. The restaurant rapidly garnered attention shortly after opening in 1972, when mobster Joe "Crazy Joe" Gallo was shot in the restaurant’s dining room. Like its mafia-related history, the food at Umberto’s is as Italian-American as it gets. Baked clams and fried calamari are the appetizer list’s biggest show-stoppers, while superbly chilled clams on the half-shell pair exquisitely with equally cold (and generously sized) cocktails from the bar. Seafood-focused mains are the name of the game here, including the garlicky linguini and clam sauce and recently resurfaced scungilli with pasta served with piping hot red sauce.

    Address: 132 Mulberry Street, Fresh York, NY 10013.

    For Italian-American eats in a less stereotypically Little Italy ambiance, Il Cortile is the way to go. Contrary to the old school Italian vibes found in the majority of the neighborhood’s restaurants, Il Cortile’s atrium-style glass ceiling and plant-filled room feel more like dining al fresco in Trastevere than the heart of Mulberry Street. The family-owned restaurant’s neighborhood roots date back to 1975, with a solid focus on Northern Italian cuisine. The homemade cheese ravioli and wood-fired pizzas are always a safe bet, though for meat lovers, springing for the Fettuccine di Parma made with sweet sausage and wild mushrooms won’t disappoint—and be sure to save room for the pillowy soft tiramisu made with creamy mascarpone and imported Italian ladyfingers drenched in espresso.

    Address: 125 Mulberry St, New York, NY 10013.

    It has been revealed that original Vincent’s, often called The Original Vincent’s Clam Bar, is home to one of the richest restaurant success stories in Little Italy. Founded in 1904 by Giuseppe and Carmela Siano, the business began as a sidewalk street cart serving up fresh seafood and jars of homemade red sauce, available in mild, medium, and hot. Today, the restaurant sits on the corner of Mott and Hester Streets, and is still known for its signature gravies, baked clams, and linguini-based pasta dishes (don’t skip the frutti di mare). As in its earliest days, Original Vincent’s still sells jars of their red sauce to-go, making replicating the restaurant’s pasta dishes at home a breeze—simply grab a bottle of Chianti, cue up your Louis Primo playlist and voila.

    Address: 119 Mott St, New York, NY 10013.

    Paesano of Mulberry Street is home to one of the coziest interiors in Little Italy, offering a peaceful refuge from the neighborhood bustle. Rustic twig bunches and leafy plants strung with twinkle lights hang from the ceiling, while traditional Italian frescos and framed family photographs adorn the whitewashed brick walls. Originally opened in 1961, the restaurant remains owned by the same family and continues to be known for their Southern Italian recipes, including linguini with clam sauce, wood-fired pizzas, and savory chicken marsala drenched in sautéed mushrooms. Meat lovers, don’t skip the restaurant’s signature Veal A La Paesano, featuring a juicy and tender veal base layered with thin slices of prosciutto, steamed broccoli, and gooey mozzarella cheese finished with succulent brown gravy.

    Address: 136 Mulberry St, Newly introduced York, NY 10013.

    Industry observers note that for serious pizza lovers, a trip to Lombardi’s is a no-brainer. Tucked on the corner of Mott and Spring, this neighborhood institution is credited as America’s first pizzeria, originally founded by Gennaro Lombardi in 1905. Lombardi quickly rose to fame for his large, heavily-topped pies, which he baked in an on-site, coal-and-gas oven. The result? Smoky crusts topped with perfectly balanced tomato sauce and gobs of whole milk mozzarella—along with sweet Italian sausage and various other accoutrements. The interior oozes with classic Fresh York charm, featuring tables clad in red-and-white checkered cloths and framed family photographs strung along the red-hued walls. Head’s up, the spot is cash only, and while there’s an ATM on site, we recommend coming prepared to avoid the withdrawal fee.

    Address: 30 Spring St, New York, NY 10012.

    It has been revealed that pasquale Jones-12_2. Brussels Sprout Pizza with Red Onion, Smoked Mozzarella & Lemon.

    In a recent development, in a sea of mediocre neighborhood wine lists, Pasqule Jones offers a breath of fresh air for Little Italy exploring wine lovers. Situated on the cusp of the neighborhood’s boundaries (and easily identifiable by its rainbow neon lights), this Italian-American pizzeria first opened its doors in 2016 and quickly became a staple for industry folks and visiting oenophiles alike. Beloved for its wood-fired Latest York style pizzas (don’t miss the signature clam pie) and thick, homemade pastas, the restaurant’s warm-yet-casual ambiance is ideal for posting up with a pie and a bottle—especially if you’re after great Burgundy, Champagne, or Italian reds. Expect classic picks from Pierre-Yves Colin-Morey, Domaine de l’Arlot, and Vietti, as well ample fun and fresh selections from Sandlands, Chacra, and Domaine Gramenon.

    Address: 187 Mulberry St, Newly introduced York, NY 10012.

    Address: 195 Grand St, New York, NY 10013.

    Recent findings suggest that although less famous than nearby Ferrara, Caffé Palermo features the innate Italian charm one looks for when wandering the neighborhood. Owned and operated by Baby John DeLutro (the self-proclaimed “Cannoli King”) since 1973, the establishment lives up to its owner’s moniker, offering flavored iterations—including pistachio and hazelnut made with sweet ricotta cream, the former of which is one of the joint’s standouts—in perfectly crisp shells. What Palermo does have over Ferrara is a solid amount of outdoor seating, ideal for posting up with a cappuccino and people watching on Mulberry.

    Address: 148 Mulberry St, Latest York, NY 10013.

    La Compagnie des Vins Surnaturels.

    If you’re looking for a wine break between pizza and pastries, this is just the ticket. Located on Little Italy's western limits (Centre Street between Broome and Grand), this French-inspired wine bar offers extensive by-the-glass options and shareable bites, including cheese and charcuterie boards to larger main courses, including beef tartare and lemon spaghetti. The comprehensive wine list, which features anywhere from 750 to 1,000+ references at all times, leans unsurprisingly French, though ample selections from Italy, Spain, and the USA are also available. Our suggestion? Post up with a bottle of Grower Champagne and relish in the perfectly executed Parisian bar à vin ambiance.

    Address: 249 Centre St, New York, NY 10013.

    Address: 409 Broome St, Fresh York, NY 10013.

    Technically located on the cusp of Little Italy’s historic boundaries (Kenmare and Broome Streets), La Esquina offers a flavor-packed reprieve from the classic red-sauce joints synonymous with the neighborhood. Situated in a former counter deli, this multi-level Mexican hotspot is best known for its casual taqueria (located in ‘The Corner Deli’ space) serving tacos, tortas, and ceviche. However, for those looking for something a bit stronger, head through the secret door and down the stairs to find the restaurant’s underground speakeasy. Lit by candle and adorned with Lucha Libre posters, the bar’s high-energy ambiance is prime for enjoying queso fundido and smoky Mexican street corn (elotes callejeros) washed down with expertly crafted agave-based cocktails.

    Address: 114 Kenmare St, New York, NY 10012.

  • Coverage typically requires you to pay upfront and then file a claim for reimbursement, and it is secondary to any compensation provided by the airline or other sources.
  • Policies differ in how soon coverage begins, the maximum reimbursement allowed, and whether limits apply per traveler or per trip, which can significantly impact families or groups.

  • Coverage usually requires a minimum delay of six hours or an overnight stay, and only applies to specific causes like bad weather or equipment failure.

  • Claim limits and eligible family members differ; some cards restrict the number of claims per year or define covered travelers more narrowly.

    Rep. James Comer rolls out 2027 bid for Kentucky governor

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • James Comer, here talking to reporters on Capitol Hill in June, is running for governor.
    • In a recent development, kentucky Rep.
    • Industry observers note that the Republican, who was just elected to a sixth full term representing Kentucky’s 1st District, is seeking to succeed term-limited Democratic Gov.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Kentucky Rep. James Comer, here talking to reporters on Capitol Hill in June, is running for governor. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    In a recent development, kentucky Rep. James R. Comer, whose role as chairman of the House Oversight Committee gave him a powerful platform to investigate Democrats, including former Presidents Joe Biden and Bill Clinton, has released a run for governor next year.

    Industry observers note that the Republican, who was just elected to a sixth full term representing Kentucky’s 1st District, is seeking to succeed term-limited Democratic Gov. Andy Beshear. Kentucky is one of three states holding off-year gubernatorial elections in 2027, alongside Louisiana and Mississippi.

    In his announcement at a tele-town hall Monday night, Comey emphasized pocketbook concerns, pledging to eliminate the state income tax and boost job-creation in Louisville.

    “If we get that income tax to zero, people are going to have more money to spend, and we're going to be able to attract more good-paying jobs to Kentucky, which will be able to keep our best and brightest in the state,’’ he stated.

    Industry observers note that as the leader of the House Oversight panel, Comer has been at the forefront in the fight over the release of records related to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. (Last week, the committee released a report concluding that the federal government mishandled criminal probes into Epstein’s activities.).

    Comer is a staunch ally of President Donald Trump, who carried Kentucky by 31 points in 2024, and his hard-nosed style of politics is conveyed in a soft-spoken Southern drawl.

    According to recent reports, known back home as Jamie, Comer has deep roots in rural Monroe County, dating back to the late 1700s. Prior to coming to Congress, he operated a farm before serving 11 years in the Kentucky House. In 2011, he was elected as the commonwealth’s commissioner of agriculture.

    He made an unsuccessful run for governor in 2015, losing the Republican primary by 83 votes to Matt Bevin, who went on to win the general election. The following year, Comer easily won election to the House from his western Kentucky district, succeeding Republican Ed Whitfield.

    Comer has moved quickly to consolidate GOP support for his gubernatorial bid. He already has the backing of Kentucky Sen. Rand Paul and Sen.-elect Andy Barr. Michael Adams, Kentucky’s term-limited secretary of state who’d been seen a potential contender, gave Comer an early endorsement this summer.

    Recent findings suggest that while Comer enters the race as the Republican front-runner, he won’t have the field to himself. Other declared hopefuls include local prosecutor Rick Hardin and distiller Charles “Bruiser” Martin, who appeared on the Discovery Channel show “Moonshiners: Master Distiller.”.

    According to recent reports, while Kentucky has in recent decades grown reliably Republican at the federal level, the GOP has won just two gubernatorial elections there over the past half century. Two high-profile Democrats have already released bids to keep the governor’s mansion in party hands: Lt. Gov. Jacqueline Coleman and former state House Majority Leader and Beshear adviser Rocky Adkins, who ran for governor in 2019.

    In a statement Tuesday, the Democratic Governors Association dismissed Comer as “a job-killing, pro-war politician who looks down on everyday Kentuckians.”.

    📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4110 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cntraveler

    ⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
