    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Americans should expect their federal agencies to be staffed by experts who gather evidence meticulously before proposing regulations disinterestedly.
    • Last month, the FTC ordered nine major companies — Delta Air Lines, Uber, and Instacart among them — “to provide detailed information that will allow the agency to study the use of personal data to set prices and compensation.” The agency, however, seems to have reached its conclusions already, given the contents of both its order and an enforcement policy proposed in August, which appears partial against personalized pricing and the businesses that employ it.
    • Vladlena Klymova is a policy analyst at the Taxpayers Protection Alliance.

    Americans should expect their federal agencies to be staffed by experts who gather evidence meticulously before proposing regulations disinterestedly. But that’s not what the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) has done when it comes to personalized pricing.

    Last month, the FTC ordered nine major companies — Delta Air Lines, Uber, and Instacart among them — “to provide detailed information that will allow the agency to study the use of personal data to set prices and compensation.” The agency, however, seems to have reached its conclusions already, given the contents of both its order and an enforcement policy proposed in August, which appears partial against personalized pricing and the businesses that employ it.

    Vladlena Klymova is a policy analyst at the Taxpayers Protection Alliance.

    #77154. Third Time’s Not The Charm: A SWISS A220’s Odd Triple Aborted Takeoff

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (958 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Onemileatatime ↗ Open Full Page

    Third Time’s Not The Charm: A SWISS A220’s Odd Triple Aborted Takeoff

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (958 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, if you’re a frequent flyer, odds are that you’ve encountered an aborted takeoff, whereby the plane accelerates down the runway, only to slow down, and eventually come to a stop.
    • However, here’s something you don’t often see — a SWISS Airbus A220 aborted its takeoff three times in a row, before finally returning to the gate to see what was going on, as reported by Blick.
    • In a recent development, on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, SWISS flight LX2110 was scheduled to operate from Zurich (ZRH) to Malaga (AGP), with a 9:35AM departure.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, if you’re a frequent flyer, odds are that you’ve encountered an aborted takeoff, whereby the plane accelerates down the runway, only to slow down, and eventually come to a stop. In some cases this can feel like a non-event, while in other cases it can feel much scarier, depending on the speed at which the takeoff is aborted.

    However, here’s something you don’t often see — a SWISS Airbus A220 aborted its takeoff three times in a row, before finally returning to the gate to see what was going on, as reported by Blick. The explanation is actually quite logical, but that doesn’t make the whole ordeal any less unusual.

    In a recent development, on Tuesday, November 17, 2026, SWISS flight LX2110 was scheduled to operate from Zurich (ZRH) to Malaga (AGP), with a 9:35AM departure. The flight was operated by an Airbus A220-300 with the registration code HB-JCM.

    The plane pushed back and taxied out to the runway right on schedule. The pilots began the takeoff roll, but then rapidly applied the brakes, causing the plane to come to a stop, while still at a slow speed. The pilots took a moment to run checklists, and then decided on another takeoff attempt, only for the same thing to happen again!

    After the second aborted takeoff, the captain reportedly informed passengers that the thrust levers had popped out during the takeoff roll, and that was the reason for the aborted takeoff. However, rather than returning to the gate, they decided to attempt an additional takeoff roll.

    It has been revealed that once again, the takeoff was aborted. At that point the captain explained that nothing like this had ever happened to him before in his 12 year career, and that the plane would be returning to the gate.

    There ended up being a plane change, and then the A220 with the registration code HB-JCO was assigned to operate this flight — it ended up taking off at 1:29PM and landing at 3:52PM, around 3.5 hours behind schedule.

    A SWISS spokesperson confirmed the incident happened, though noted that the takeoffs were aborted at a low speed of around 50 kilometers per hour (around 30 miles per hour).

    Recent findings suggest that what explains the aborted takeoffs? Well, it was because as the plane accelerated for takeoff, the automatic thrust control system automatically deactivated. To explain this as simply as possible, as I understand it, on the A220 when the auto-thrust is armed and the thrust levers are moved forward for takeoff, the auto-thrust then takes over, and moves the levers forward without manual intervention.

    According to recent reports, in other words, one of the pilots keeps their hands on the auto-thrust levers and “moves” with them, but doesn’t actually apply any force. Pilots are trained this way, and to not manually apply force. In the event that the crew tries to stop the auto-thrust lever motion, a pressure switch detects this, and then disengages the auto-thrust, to allow for a manual override.

    In this case, the auto-thrust incorrectly detected resistance, when the pilots weren’t attempting to apply it. According to the airline, the system that monitors the aircraft’s technical status in real time was unable to identify the cause of the error, as no errors were displayed in the system. So at first, the pilots likely wondered if they had accidentally applied force.

    However, once technicians had a look at the plane, it was discovered that the switch for disabling the automatic thrust control on the original aircraft was stuck, and this caused the automatic thrust control to shut down during takeoff attempts.

    So while this can understandably seem scary to passengers, this wasn’t even a direct safety problem. After all, the pilots could’ve also manually moved the throttles. However, you also don’t want to take off when you know there’s an issue with the throttles, since that’s not exactly a best practice.

    A SWISS Airbus A220 attempted a takeoff from Zurich three times in a row. While I’ve had two consecutive aborted takeoffs, I’ve never had three, and I can’t imagine that happens all too often.

    It has been revealed that while this is unusual, it sounds like this was handled well, and I can see why the pilots kept trying. This wasn’t a critical safety concern, but instead, just an incorrect detection of inputs, in a way that wouldn’t really pose a risk to the flight. At the same time, you don’t want to knowingly take off with a fault switch.

    What do you make of this SWISS aborted takeoff trio?

    Sources indicate that A Southwest Airlines passenger indicates she was settled into an exit row window seat in Las Vegas, pleased about the empty middle seat beside her, when the crew began looking for her husband. Instead, she was escorted off the roughly 9 p.m. flight to Boise and quoted about $400 for a departure the next morning. Southwest was right about the Companion Pass rule. Surely though it shouldn’t take materially longer to sell a ticket than to remove a passenger. She’d spent four days in Las Vegas, checked two 50 pound bags, and was ready to get home. Sitting in row 14, she’d already given the flight attendant her verbal agreement to help with the emergency exit. Her headphones were on. She was listening to an audiobook and playing a game on her phone. Then came the announcement asking Mr. Batis to identify himself. She told the crew he wasn’t on board and wouldn’t be joining them. That’s when she realized why the middle seat was empty. An employee came back to her row and explained that her free ticket depended on her husband actually taking the flight. Well, can I just pay with a credit card? … I’ve been a Southwest card member for 20 plus years. I have my own points. Can I just book it, you know, pay for it now? She says he told her they were ready to push back. He left, returned about three minutes later, and told her she’d have to get off. She gathered her things and went with him. I think he was expecting, like, some complete chaos. @angiebatis — Her account of being removed from the Southwest flight Companion Pass Requires The Passholder To Travel I’ve been a Companion Pass holder, including through promotions, and it’s still an extraordinary deal. Book your own Southwest flight with money or points, then add your designated companion for taxes and fees starting at $5.60 each way, as long as there’s a seat available. The free travel is tied to accompanying the passholder. Her husband paid for a ticket, which then supports the companion’s ticket. The rules though are very clear: If the Companion is not traveling with the Member, the Companion’s reservation will be canceled. I’ve covered almost this exact situation before. In June 2024, a companion boarded Southwest flight 2097 from Savannah to Baltimore. The passholder canceled his own ticket just before departure. Southwest removed the companion, conducting a manual boarding pass check to find her in the days before assigned seating. That case involved a cancellation and an apparent attempt to get the companion transported while refunding the underlying ticket. Here the passenger was fully willing to pay. I don’t think she was actually trying to scam the airline, though she’d be traveling free (and if her husband did cancel in time prior to departure he’d still have his flight credit to use). The requirement to fly together isn’t one of the changes Southwest is making to Companion Pass in 2027. It’s been a longstanding requirement. She Offered To Pay For The Seat Comments on the woman’s video between people who think a longtime Southwest customer should know how the pass works and people who think the airline should have found a way to get her home. It’s probably just best that she got off without making a scene. Several viewers ask why this wasn’t caught at check-in or at the gate. But checking in isn’t the same as boarding. If her husband wasn’t checked in though it should get caught at the check-in deadline. He may have been checked in and just didn’t board. There’s an interesting bit of history here. This same woman went viral in 2024 praising a Southwest gate agent in Phoenix. She filmed herself thanking an employee named Krista for her kindness. In this video, she also thanks the gate agent and tells her it isn’t her fault. Her host at the Venetian arranged a chauffeur, another room, dinner and a car back to the airport. She was still separated from her checked bags, without a phone charging cord or a brush. I bet her casino host could manage that… So this was day old hair yesterday. Today it’s two day old hair. …I was embarrassed, I was humiliated, I was mad at my husband, the whole thing.     📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    I’ve gotta say, huge kudos to Mexico’s President, Claudia Sheinbaum, for setting quite the example in terms of how she recently traveled to China, as flagged by View from the Wing….

    Sources indicate that world leaders have just met in Shenzhen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting. As you’d expect, most leaders flew on their government planes. There were some exceptions, though I can’t imagine anyone else flew the same way as Mexico’s 64-year-old president.

    Viajamos hacia Shenzhen para representar a México en el Foro de Cooperación Económica Asia-Pacífico (APEC) China 2026; la agenda de actividades incluye reunión con empresarios de países miembros. Además, participaré en la conferencia de prensa matutina para informar avances de… pic.twitter.com/F9UqRLjFlb.

    According to recent reports, media reports suggest she flew to China on China Southern. Specifically, she traveled on Sunday, November 15, 2026, on CZ8032, from Mexico City (MEX) to Shenzhen (SZX), with a refueling stop in Tijuana (TIJ), and the journey covering a distance of 8,803 miles.

    Sources indicate that the Airbus A350-900 took off from Mexico City at 12:49AM, arriving in Tijuana at 2:02AM, after a flight time of 3hr13min. Then it took off again at 4:34AM, and landed in Shenzhen the following morning at 11:31AM, after a flight time of 14hr56min. All-in-all, the flight took around 21 hours, including the refueling stop.

    The shocking thing here isn’t that she traveled commercial, but instead, that she reportedly flew in economy! Reports suggest she was in seat 33B, which would be a middle seat in economy, no less!

    Llegamos a la Ciudad de México en el vuelo CZ8031 desde Shenzhen, China. Agradecemos a toda la tripulación por su apoyo. pic.twitter.com/DSC83CpnDQ.

    I think a head of state should reasonably be able to fly business class on a flight of this length, for two reasons:.

    That being remarked, I absolutely commend her for the example she is setting. It’s certainly quite a contrast to what we’ve seen here, where President Trump accepted a Boeing 747-8 as a gift from Qatar, and talked about how he has done it to make Americans be proud, because “our country has to be represented properly.” Heck, just this week he talked about “China was very impressed” and “Russia was very impressed” of his new plane. Lovely, I’m happy we’re impressing Putin, that makes me proud to be an American!

    "Russia was very impressed" — Trump leads his press conference by bragging about taking the longest flight in Air Force One history, in case you were worried that he actually accomplished something useful on his trip pic.twitter.com/dDIHg8wb1w.

    Sources indicate that keep in mind that Mexico has an interesting history when it comes to how leaders fly. In 2016, Mexico’s government took control of a private Boeing 787, which flew around former President Enrique Pena Nieto. The purchase of the plane had actually been arranged under the previous president, Felipe Calderón, in 2012.

    Industry observers note that then in 2018, when Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador took charge in Mexico, he fulfilled a campaign promise of selling that 787, which turned out to be pretty challenging, given that demand for a secondhand VIP 787 isn’t exactly that high (the plane ended up going to Tajikistan). Sheinbaum has kept that general legacy going, by flying commercial.

    According to recent reports, mexico’s President, Claudia Sheinbaum, traveled to the recent summit in China differently than virtually all other government leaders. Not only did she fly commercial, but she traveled in economy, and reportedly even in a middle seat.

    There’s no denying that this is more about optics than anything, but I very much respect that. It’s nice to see heads of state who lead by example, as it’s pretty rare to see nowadays.

    Bilt Offers JetBlue Elite Status For December Rent Day—With A Fast Track To Keep It Through 2027

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 50 min read (10020 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~50 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Bilt’s December Rent Day offers a three month trial of JetBlue elite status, with a much easier path to keeping it through January 2028.
    • When Bilt added JetBlue as a transfer partner last month, I wrote that status matches could be coming.
    • There’s also up to a 100% bonus redeeming Bilt points for credit card statement credits, a targeted spending offer, and Brittany Snow playing Rent Free.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Bilt’s December Rent Day offers a three month trial of JetBlue elite status, with a much easier path to keeping it through January 2028. Silver and Gold members get Mosaic 1 at no points cost. Platinum members start at Mosaic 2, which means EvenMore seats at booking instead of waiting until closer to departure. When Bilt added JetBlue as a transfer partner last month, I wrote that status matches could be coming. You qualify based on your Bilt status, so you don’t need to bring elite status from another airline. There’s also up to a 100% bonus redeeming Bilt points for credit card statement credits, a targeted spending offer, and Brittany Snow playing Rent Free. I have no idea who she is. I’m much more interested in the JetBlue offer than cashing out Bilt points at under 1.5 cents apiece. Three Months Of JetBlue Status, With A Path Through January 2028 Here’s the initial status offered: Bilt Status   JetBlue Trial Status   Points Requirement Blue Mosaic 1 10,000 Bilt points Silver Mosaic 1 None Gold Mosaic 1 None Platinum Mosaic 2 None Blue members have to transfer 10,000 points to trigger the match. Everyone has three months after receiving the matched status to earn and receive enough qualifying tiles to extend it through January 31, 2028: Status Earned   Challenge Requirement   Normal Annual Requirement Mosaic 1 10 tiles 50 tiles Mosaic 2 25 tiles 100 tiles Mosaic 3 40 tiles 150 tiles Under JetBlue’s normal earning rules, a tile takes $100 in qualifying spending on flights, JetBlue Vacations or TrueBlue Travel, or $1,000 in JetBlue credit card spending. So the travel equivalents are $1,000, $2,500 and $4,000. Taxes and fees don’t count. The corresponding spend amounts would be $10,000, $25,000 and $40,000, or you could combine tiles from travel and card spending. Spending on a Bilt card isn’t JetBlue card spending. You can earn JetBlue tiles via travel on JetBlue, United Airlines, JetBlue Vacations; cobrand card spend; purchased or earned bonus tiles (but gifted tiles don’t count); and the annual 25 Tile Bonus awarded to JetBlue Premier Wcardmembers. Folks who have received a past JetBlue challenge are eligible for this offer. Where The Status Is Most Useful The immediate value is better seating and fewer fees on trips you already intend to take. Mosaic 1 includes one checked bag, priority services, eligible same-day switches, and complimentary EvenMore selection starting 36 hours before departure for the member and up to two companions, subject to availability. Mosaic 2 adds a second checked bag and moves EvenMore selection to booking for the member and up to two companions. Mosaic 3 includes four Premium Upgrade Certificates, the upcoming name for Move to Mint certificates (and those meeting the challenge requirements will receive them). Main Base fares exclude important seating benefits. And Mosaic 1 through 3 don’t include Mosaic 4 lounge access. JetBlue has also announced complimentary upgrades to its new BlueFirst domestic first class for all Mosaic tiers as equipped aircraft enter service. These are space available upgrades, with higher Mosaic levels ahead of lower ones. Main Base and EvenMore Base fares don’t qualify. Premium Upgrade Certificates can confirm Mint or BlueFirst, including on eligible TrueBlue points tickets. Four certificates don’t necessarily mean four upgrades because the number required varies by flight. Starting February 1, JetBlue will also let Mosaic 2 members select a certificate through Perks You Pick. I’ve asked whether matched members get that selection. There’s A United Airlines Angle, Too Under JetBlue’s Blue Sky partnership, Mosaic members receive benefits on eligible United Airlines trips booked through JetBlue, including a checked bag, preferred seats after booking and Economy Plus at check-in. Mosaic 1 gets Group 2 boarding, while Mosaic 2 and above get Group 1. United flights booked through JetBlue also earn tiles under the ordinary program. So you can keep JetBlue status through travel on United. There’s No Transfer Bonus Bilt points transfer to JetBlue at 1:1. This December announcement doesn’t include a bonus on those transfers. I’m generally not moving Bilt points to JetBlue for ordinary redemptions worth around 1.3 cents apiece. One option worth comparing is a regular paid JetBlue ticket purchased through Bilt’s portal using points. Under ordinary revenue-ticket rules, that should earn tiles, whereas transferring points into TrueBlue doesn’t earn tiles. Portal bookings do give up JetBlue’s direct-booking points bonus. The more interesting transfer uses remain partner business class awards, such as the 54,000-point Condor business class awards from the East Coast to Frankfurt I’ve covered, when available. Mosaic doesn’t add benefits to a Condor flight. If you already have the JetBlue Premier card, its 15% award rebate includes partner flights. A 54,000-point award returns 8,100 TrueBlue points, for a net cost of 45,900. You need all 54,000 upfront, and the rebate comes back as JetBlue points, not Bilt points. A 100% Statement Credit Bonus Still Only Gets You About 1.1 Cents Eligible cardholders get increased statement credit redemption value from November 20 at 9 a.m. Eastern through December 2 at 2:59 a.m. Eastern. The minimum redemption is 1,000 points. This bonus depends on which Bilt credit card you have, not your Bilt elite status. At the usual 0.55-cent statement credit redemption rate, the math is: Bilt Card   Bonus   Value Per Point   Credit For 10,000 Points Blue 25% 0.6875 cents $68.75 Obsidian 50% 0.825 cents $82.50 Palladium 100% 1.1 cents $110 I wouldn’t do this. Even Palladium’s doubled rate is less than the $125 in travel those same 10,000 points buy through Bilt, before considering Hyatt or airline transfers. I passed on last month’s gift card bonus, too. Two Separate Opportunities To Earn 1,000 Extra Points Some cardholders will receive a targeted offer for 1,000 bonus points after $500 in everyday purchases from November 20 at 9 a.m. Eastern through November 30 at 11:59 p.m. Eastern. Rent and mortgage payments don’t count. Check your account for eligibility. Then the usual Rent Day double points apply on December 1, with a cap of 1,000 additional points: Bilt Blue: 2 points per dollar on everyday spending. Bilt Obsidian: 6 points in your selected dining or grocery category, 4 on travel and 2 on other everyday spending. Bilt Palladium: 4 points per dollar on everyday spending. Rent and tax payments don’t qualify for the extra points (tax payments usually don’t earn at all). On Palladium, $500 in eligible December 1 spending earns the full 1,000-point Rent Day bonus on top of the usual 1,000 points. The holiday shopping offer ends the night before Rent Day. The same purchase can’t satisfy both offers. A targeted Palladium member with $500 of ordinary spending before the deadline and another $500 on December 1 could earn 2,000 promotional bonus points across the two. Brittany Snow, Free Rent And December Experiences Brittany Snow is this month’s Rent Free guest. The game opens November 20 at noon Eastern and closes December 1 at 3 p.m. Eastern, with results after 4 p.m. The top 10 members win a month’s rent up to $2,500, with additional rent winners depending on how well she does. Rent winners also get a signed copy of September Letters. The next 100 receive 1,000 points and the next 500 receive 100 points. There’s also a November 22 brunch with Snow and September Letters co-founder Jaspre Guest at The Twenty Two in New York, from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. It’s $45 or 3,000 points, includes bites and cocktails, and opens for booking November 20 at 9 a.m. Eastern. Guests must be at least 21. The booking is final sale. The book itself is $20 or 2,000 points, with 100 copies available beginning November 20 at 9 a.m. Eastern. Members can apply up to $20 of their monthly Bilt Cash allowance. I’d use available Bilt Cash rather than redeem points at a penny each. Shipping is expected in two to three weeks, and sales are final. Members can write letters through the app, choosing whether to keep them private or share them. Select Bilt Alliance buildings will also have September Letters mailboxes, with letters mailed back to their writers in a year. Bookings for the following experiences open Saturday, November 21 at 11:50 a.m. Eastern for Gold and Platinum, and noon for everyone else: Dining: December 1 meals at 40 restaurants across nine cities. Most cost $35–$78 or 2,500–5,000 points. There are three-course menus at most venues, four courses at Hutong and omakase at seven Bondi locations. Drink add-ons cost $20–$46 and must be purchased when booking. Up to $50 Bilt Cash can be applied to one dining experience, with the rest paid in cash. Book by November 30 at 5 p.m. Eastern. There’s also first access to American Cut’s December 31 cocktail party in New York at 6 p.m., priced at $250, with 20 seats. Comedy: 20 highlights December 4–19. Club experiences cost $40 or 2,500 points, except Mic Drop MANIA in Chandler at $30 or 2,000 points, with two drinks included. Premium experiences cost $75 or 5,000 points and include two drinks and light bites. Austin’s The Creek & The Cave is among the venues. Members can use up to $50 Bilt Cash toward a comedy show for the month. Booking closes at 11 a.m. Eastern on the show date, or when sold out. Fitness: Free December 1 SoulCycle and Barry’s classes, with 1,175 and 580 spots respectively. Bookings close November 30 at 7 p.m. Eastern. Dining allows four seats per member per booking, and comedy allows four tickets per person. These experiences are final sale. I’d use Bilt Cash before points: a common $60 dinner costs 4,000 points, but applying $50 Bilt Cash leaves $10 to pay and keeps your points available for travel. And on December 1, Bilt’s cafe at 837 Washington Street in New York will offer members a complimentary Daniel Boulud tasting from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. Eastern: lobster vol-au-vent (with a vegetarian option), warm apple chausson, a hot chocolate shake and warm spiced cider.     According to recent reports, here’s the initial status offered: Bilt Status   JetBlue Trial Status   Points Requirement Blue Mosaic 1 10,000 Bilt points Silver Mosaic 1 None Gold Mosaic 1 None Platinum Mosaic 2 None Blue members have to transfer 10,000 points to trigger the match. Everyone has three months after receiving the matched status to earn and receive enough qualifying tiles to extend it through January 31, 2028: Status Earned   Challenge Requirement   Normal Annual Requirement Mosaic 1 10 tiles 50 tiles Mosaic 2 25 tiles 100 tiles Mosaic 3 40 tiles 150 tiles Under JetBlue’s normal earning rules, a tile takes $100 in qualifying spending on flights, JetBlue Vacations or TrueBlue Travel, or $1,000 in JetBlue credit card spending. So the travel equivalents are $1,000, $2,500 and $4,000. Taxes and fees don’t count. The corresponding spend amounts would be $10,000, $25,000 and $40,000, or you could combine tiles from travel and card spending. Spending on a Bilt card isn’t JetBlue card spending. You can earn JetBlue tiles via travel on JetBlue, United Airlines, JetBlue Vacations; cobrand card spend; purchased or earned bonus tiles (but gifted tiles don’t count); and the annual 25 Tile Bonus awarded to JetBlue Premier Wcardmembers. Folks who have received a past JetBlue challenge are eligible for this offer. Where The Status Is Most Useful The immediate value is better seating and fewer fees on trips you already intend to take. Mosaic 1 includes one checked bag, priority services, eligible same-day switches, and complimentary EvenMore selection starting 36 hours before departure for the member and up to two companions, subject to availability. Mosaic 2 adds a second checked bag and moves EvenMore selection to booking for the member and up to two companions. Mosaic 3 includes four Premium Upgrade Certificates, the upcoming name for Move to Mint certificates (and those meeting the challenge requirements will receive them). Main Base fares exclude notable seating benefits. And Mosaic 1 through 3 don’t include Mosaic 4 lounge access. JetBlue has also announced complimentary upgrades to its new BlueFirst domestic first class for all Mosaic tiers as equipped aircraft enter service. These are space available upgrades, with higher Mosaic levels ahead of lower ones. Main Base and EvenMore Base fares don’t qualify. Premium Upgrade Certificates can confirm Mint or BlueFirst, including on eligible TrueBlue points tickets. Four certificates don’t necessarily mean four upgrades because the number required varies by flight. Starting February 1, JetBlue will also let Mosaic 2 members select a certificate through Perks You Pick. I’ve asked whether matched members get that selection. There’s A United Airlines Angle, Too Under JetBlue’s Blue Sky partnership, Mosaic members receive benefits on eligible United Airlines trips booked through JetBlue, including a checked bag, preferred seats after booking and Economy Plus at check-in. Mosaic 1 gets Group 2 boarding, while Mosaic 2 and above get Group 1. United flights booked through JetBlue also earn tiles under the ordinary program. So you can keep JetBlue status through travel on United. There’s No Transfer Bonus Bilt points transfer to JetBlue at 1:1. This December announcement doesn’t include a bonus on those transfers. I’m generally not moving Bilt points to JetBlue for ordinary redemptions worth around 1.3 cents apiece. One option worth comparing is a regular paid JetBlue ticket purchased through Bilt’s portal using points. Under ordinary revenue-ticket rules, that should earn tiles, whereas transferring points into TrueBlue doesn’t earn tiles. Portal bookings do give up JetBlue’s direct-booking points bonus. The more interesting transfer uses remain partner business class awards, such as the 54,000-point Condor business class awards from the East Coast to Frankfurt I’ve covered, when available. Mosaic doesn’t add benefits to a Condor flight. If you already have the JetBlue Premier card, its 15% award rebate includes partner flights. A 54,000-point award returns 8,100 TrueBlue points, for a net cost of 45,900. You need all 54,000 upfront, and the rebate comes back as JetBlue points, not Bilt points. A 100% Statement Credit Bonus Still Only Gets You About 1.1 Cents Eligible cardholders get increased statement credit redemption value from November 20 at 9 a.m. Eastern through December 2 at 2:59 a.m. Eastern. The minimum redemption is 1,000 points. This bonus depends on which Bilt credit card you have, not your Bilt elite status. At the usual 0.55-cent statement credit redemption rate, the math is: Bilt Card   Bonus   Value Per Point   Credit For 10,000 Points Blue 25% 0.6875 cents $68.75 Obsidian 50% 0.825 cents $82.50 Palladium 100% 1.1 cents $110 I wouldn’t do this. Even Palladium’s doubled rate is less than the $125 in travel those same 10,000 points buy through Bilt, before considering Hyatt or airline transfers. I passed on last month’s gift card bonus, too. Two Separate Opportunities To Earn 1,000 Extra Points Some cardholders will receive a targeted offer for 1,000 bonus points after $500 in everyday purchases from November 20 at 9 a.m. Eastern through November 30 at 11:59 p.m. Eastern. Rent and mortgage payments don’t count. Check your account for eligibility. Then the usual Rent Day double points apply on December 1, with a cap of 1,000 additional points: Bilt Blue: 2 points per dollar on everyday spending. Bilt Obsidian: 6 points in your selected dining or grocery category, 4 on travel and 2 on other everyday spending. Bilt Palladium: 4 points per dollar on everyday spending. Rent and tax payments don’t qualify for the extra points (tax payments usually don’t earn at all). On Palladium, $500 in eligible December 1 spending earns the full 1,000-point Rent Day bonus on top of the usual 1,000 points. The holiday shopping offer ends the night before Rent Day. The same purchase can’t satisfy both offers. A targeted Palladium member with $500 of ordinary spending before the deadline and another $500 on December 1 could earn 2,000 promotional bonus points across the two. Brittany Snow, Free Rent And December Experiences Brittany Snow is this month’s Rent Free guest. The game opens November 20 at noon Eastern and closes December 1 at 3 p.m. Eastern, with results after 4 p.m. The top 10 members win a month’s rent up to $2,500, with additional rent winners depending on how well she does. Rent winners also get a signed copy of September Letters. The next 100 receive 1,000 points and the next 500 receive 100 points. There’s also a November 22 brunch with Snow and September Letters co-founder Jaspre Guest at The Twenty Two in New York, from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. It’s $45 or 3,000 points, includes bites and cocktails, and opens for booking November 20 at 9 a.m. Eastern. Guests must be at least 21. The booking is final sale. The book itself is $20 or 2,000 points, with 100 copies available beginning November 20 at 9 a.m. Eastern. Members can apply up to $20 of their monthly Bilt Cash allowance. I’d use available Bilt Cash rather than redeem points at a penny each. Shipping is expected in two to three weeks, and sales are final. Members can write letters through the app, choosing whether to keep them private or share them. Select Bilt Alliance buildings will also have September Letters mailboxes, with letters mailed back to their writers in a year. Bookings for the following experiences open Saturday, November 21 at 11:50 a.m. Eastern for Gold and Platinum, and noon for everyone else: Dining: December 1 meals at 40 restaurants across nine cities. Most cost $35–$78 or 2,500–5,000 points. There are three-course menus at most venues, four courses at Hutong and omakase at seven Bondi locations. Drink add-ons cost $20–$46 and must be purchased when booking. Up to $50 Bilt Cash can be applied to one dining experience, with the rest paid in cash. Book by November 30 at 5 p.m. Eastern. There’s also first access to American Cut’s December 31 cocktail party in New York at 6 p.m., priced at $250, with 20 seats. Comedy: 20 shows December 4–19. Club experiences cost $40 or 2,500 points, except Mic Drop MANIA in Chandler at $30 or 2,000 points, with two drinks included. Premium experiences cost $75 or 5,000 points and include two drinks and light bites. Austin’s The Creek & The Cave is among the venues. Members can use up to $50 Bilt Cash toward a comedy show for the month. Booking closes at 11 a.m. Eastern on the show date, or when sold out. Fitness: Free December 1 SoulCycle and Barry’s classes, with 1,175 and 580 spots respectively. Bookings close November 30 at 7 p.m. Eastern. Dining allows four seats per member per booking, and comedy allows four tickets per person. These experiences are final sale. I’d use Bilt Cash before points: a common $60 dinner costs 4,000 points, but applying $50 Bilt Cash leaves $10 to pay and keeps your points available for travel. And on December 1, Bilt’s cafe at 837 Washington Street in New York will offer members a complimentary Daniel Boulud tasting from 11 a.m. to 5 p.m. Eastern: lobster vol-au-vent (with a vegetarian option), warm apple chausson, a hot chocolate shake and warm spiced cider.     #77148. An Overhyped Trilateral Summit

    📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (951 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nationalreview ↗ Open Full Page

    An Overhyped Trilateral Summit

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (951 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nationalreview

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Donald Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin have now concluded their first-ever trilateral meeting.
    • That is not to deny that some of the optics involved were grating.
    • Industry observers note that the fact that Putin was in the room has attracted criticism for its symbolic “confirmation” of Russia as one of, to borrow a term from the real Yalta, the “major three.” Not so much: Putin’s presence merely reflected geopolitical reality, something that, however unpleasant, cannot be wished away.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Donald Trump, Xi Jinping, and Vladimir Putin have now concluded their first-ever trilateral meeting. Each leader has pronounced himself satisfied with their discussion. But if their concluding statement is an accurate reflection of what was said in the closed session, little of any real consequence — with one possible exception — was agreed to, which was only to be expected. Much has been made by some of the symbolism of the meeting. Did it signal that a disreputable carve-up, even a new Yalta, was underway? If that was the plan, the result, appropriately and mercifully, looks like a package with more than a touch of Temu about it.

    That is not to deny that some of the optics involved were grating. Trump’s earlier, overly enthusiastic greeting of his “friend” Putin — the aggressor, after all, in a genocidal war — was not only nauseating but also careless. It sent a disturbing signal to the rest of NATO, an organization that still plays a critical role in maintaining American security as well as peace, however uneasy, in Europe west of Ukraine. It is to be hoped that Trump’s delight at the sight of his supposed pal was, to use a word often applied to this president’s approach to diplomacy, transactional, a display of a dealmaker’s schmooze and nothing more.

    Industry observers note that the fact that Putin was in the room has attracted criticism for its symbolic “confirmation” of Russia as one of, to borrow a term from the real Yalta, the “major three.” Not so much: Putin’s presence merely reflected geopolitical reality, something that, however unpleasant, cannot be wished away. Russia is economically enfeebled and embroiled in a brutally and humiliatingly debilitating war, but it remains a vast, resource-rich country that, militarily anyway, counts as a superpower and one that, as Ukrainians can testify, is still capable of wreaking immense destruction. The more interesting symbolism was detectable in the various gestures through which Xi Jinping emphasized during Putin’s visit that Russia is China’s junior partner. That, too, is today’s reality.

    Industry observers note that as alluded to above, the joint statement issued after the meeting was, as should have been expected, thin gruel. There was talk of reforming the U.N. “so that it may respond more effectively to global challenges and fulfil its fundamental mission of maintaining international peace and security.” If that implies reining in Turtle Bay’s efforts to extend supranational (and thus post-democratic) governance, that’s no bad thing, but in practice little will probably change.

    Sources indicate that in a similar vein, the trio, whose countries have not submitted to the jurisdiction of the International Criminal Court, implicitly criticized the attempted extension of its reach. They stressed the need for “respect for immunities of State officials,” a subject doubtless close to Putin’s heart. There is no need to grumble too much about this. The ICC is highly politicized, and, while it does not constitute much of a deterrent, it may even provide a perverse incentive to wrongdoers to hang onto power. Putin deserves to face judgment, but a better place for that would be Kyiv, not The Hague.

    And all three declared that they planned “to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations.” If that reflected some post-midterms unease on Trump’s part, that, as an admission of weakness, would have been a message better not sent. It would also be a mistake, despite recent waivers, for the U.S. to abandon its general application of sanctions on Iranian and Russian oil (the Europeans, incidentally, could do a better job of enforcing theirs). No pressure should be put on Ukraine to stop attacking Russian energy infrastructure other than as part of a general “energy cease-fire” such as that floated earlier this year, which Ukraine was willing to accept.

    It has been revealed that no details have been released so far of what was said in the meeting about Ukraine. However, Putin has been reiterating his hard line, supplemented by an absurd and aggressive proposal to rewrite Europe’s security architecture. Hopefully, Trump was not misled by any bonhomie in Shenzhen, although some accounts of his later call with European leaders were not entirely encouraging in that respect.

    From left: Russian President Vladimir Putin, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and U.S. President Donald Trump participate in a trilateral meeting during the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen, China, November 19, 2026.

    Recent findings suggest that to return to reality: China has no interest in helping end the war in Ukraine, and Russia’s ambitions in Europe are such that the eventual consequences of undermining Kyiv’s ability to resist won’t stop at Ukraine’s borders. Speaking of which, we hope that Trump warned Xi and Putin that the growing intensity of “gray zone” activity, from drones in Leipzig Airport to cyberattacks on both sides of the Atlantic, risks triggering retaliation that could easily spiral into something extremely dangerous.

    Any claims that the Shenzhen meeting has delivered the death blow to the post-1945 order would be overblown, akin to complaining about the murder of a corpse. The postwar settlement has been in flux for decades — Nixon, after all, went to China — a process that has accelerated, along with dramatic shifts in relative global economic and political power, since the Soviet collapse. But although the landscape has changed, Trump should pay more attention to America’s successful management of the (first) Cold War. Alliances matter, deterrence works, strength is rewarded, and aggression by, or sponsored by, hostile powers and their proxies should be contained and, where possible, reversed.

    The Editors comprise the senior editorial staff of National Review magazine and nationalreview.com.

    On “An Overhyped Trilateral Summit”.

    #77146. Why JSX Just Bought New Pacific Airlines, The Strange, Failed 757 Startup

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (977 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Onemileatatime ↗ Open Full Page

    Why JSX Just Bought New Pacific Airlines, The Strange, Failed 757 Startup

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (977 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Public charter air carrier JSX has just acquired Upcoming Pacific Airlines, and with this, New Pacific Airlines intends to resume flights, with Embraer E145 aircraft.
    • If you’re not familiar with New Pacific Airlines, you’re probably thinking “huh?” If you are familiar with New Pacific Airlines, you’re probably thinking “WTF?” There’s a sneaky and logical explanation here, so let me explain.
    • Recent findings suggest that let’s start with a little context.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Public charter air carrier JSX has just acquired Upcoming Pacific Airlines, and with this, New Pacific Airlines intends to resume flights, with Embraer E145 aircraft.

    If you’re not familiar with New Pacific Airlines, you’re probably thinking “huh?” If you are familiar with New Pacific Airlines, you’re probably thinking “WTF?” There’s a sneaky and logical explanation here, so let me explain.

    Recent findings suggest that let’s start with a little context. JSX is a public charter air carrier, which operates a fleet of nearly 60 planes, most of which are Embraer E135s and E145s.

    According to recent reports, it operates as a Part 135 operator, meaning it’s not technically an airline, as it’s using a loophole that allows it to not use standard TSA security screening, hire pilots with fewer than 1,500 hours, etc. Basically what’s happening is that one subsidiary sells the tickets, and then another subsidiary operates the flights, so it’s technically a “charter” (with 30 people who don’t know one another).

    Then there’s New Pacific Airlines, one of the strangest airline startups we’ve ever seen, and which I’ve covered extensively. The airline acquired some Boeing 757s, and the business blueprint was to connect North America and Asia via Anchorage (ANC).

    The business model made zero sense in the first place, though there was some funding there, and they even invested in constructing a lounge in Anchorage, even though those flights never did happen. The airline did briefly fly from (ONT) to Nashville (BNA) — as one does — before ultimately going out of business.

    That brings us to the news. New Pacific Airlines intends to resume flights with Embraer E145s that are leased from JSX, as reported by IshrionA. According to a Department of Transportation filing, the airline intends to resume flights with planes featuring 42 seats, which is higher than the 30-seat limit you’ll find on current JSX planes.

    According to recent reports, JSX acquires Latest Pacific Airlines.New Pacific Airlines intends to resume flights with ERJ 145 leased from JSX. pic.twitter.com/uMMS0J2fZy.

    Sources indicate that on the surface, this of course makes absolutely no sense. Fresh Pacific Airlines was out of business, and the business model made no sense. So why would JSX buy an airline and then lease planes to it?

    Long story short, this seems to be a play to acquire a cheap Part 121 certificate. A Part 121 operator is a company that’s allowed to operate scheduled air transport… in other words, a “real” airline. As I mentioned above, JSX has historically been a Part 135 operator, and that explicitly means it’s not an airline. It’s a public charter air carrier, so it’s not a “real” airline.

    Going back a couple of years, we know that the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) was considering cracking down on carriers like JSX, since they definitely don’t operate within the spirit of the rules. That’s not to say that JSX did anything wrong, because by the letter of the law, they’re following it exactly. It’s just that the letter of the law makes no sense, and clearly doesn’t reflect the intent behind distinguishing between Part 121 and Part 135 operators.

    Under Trump, there was no scrutiny of this. However, with Democrats soon controlling both the House and Senate, I imagine JSX leaders may be worried that there could again be more scrutiny. If nothing else, buying a cheap Part 121 certificate is a good insurance policy, in case the government does crack down. After all, these can basically be “sold,” while acquiring one from scratch can be grueling process.

    It has been revealed that I wouldn’t assume that anything will really operate with Fresh Pacific Airlines branding, or based on a New Pacific Airlines business model. Instead, I imagine the idea is that JSX will start dabbling in Part 121 operations, which is why these planes will have more seats (above the 30-seat cap that’s allowed), since that’s no longer a factor.

    If the government were to crack down on Part 135 operators, JSX could move to Part 121 operations. However, they’d have to make lots of changes, from their pilot hiring, to the way passengers are screened.

    Industry observers note that JSX has just bought New Pacific, the airline with an absurd business model that went bankrupt. No, JSX isn’t inspired by the concept of flying Boeing 757s to Asia. Instead, this is clearly the cheapest way for JSX to acquire a Part 121 certificate, which would be required for the carrier to continue operations in the event that the government were to crack down on the Part 135 operator loophole.

    It’s going to be interesting to see how this evolves, both since JSX seems to have plans to operate Part 121 operations in the near future, and also to see how JSX’s business model would evolve if the Part 135 concept were blocked.

    What do you make of this JSX Part 121 play?

    • In a recent development, israir at the moment flies five times a week between New York JFK and Tel Aviv.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    American Airlines hasn’t flown to Israel since the October 7, 2023 attacks. Israir is flying the route using two of American’s retired Airbus A330s. Now American is partnering with Israir to connect those passengers to its network beyond New York. In August I flagged that Israir had acquired American’s old aircraft. Now it’s getting access to more of the customers it needs to fill those planes. American, meanwhile, gets connecting passengers and an Israeli sales partner ahead of its own planned return to the Israel market. Israir currently flies five times a week between New York JFK and Tel Aviv. American aims to resume daily service March 27, 2027, using Boeing 777-200ERs. I’d covered their previous plan to return in March 2026, they’ve kept planning to return and then not, given instability in the region even as other U.S. carriers flew. Ex-American Airlines Airbus A330-200 N287AY, Credit: Anna Zvereva / Wikimedia Commons. What American And Israir Have Agreed To The initial arrangement has two parts: Israir will put its flight code on American’s JFK–Tel Aviv service. Israir can market an American-operated flight as part of its own offering when American returns. An interline agreement will connect passengers beyond JFK. Travelers crossing the Atlantic on either airline will be able to combine that flight with American connections across the United States, Canada, Latin America and the Caribbean. An interline agreement supplies the framework for selling a connecting trip on one ticket and through-checking bags. A codeshare adds another airline’s flight number to the same flight. The initial codeshare involves Israir marketing American’s flight. American hasn’t announced that it’s putting its code on Israir’s A330 service. Israir’s stock exchange filing says the agreement was signed November 19, with initial implementation targeted by the end of 2026. That depends on regulatory approvals, technology and operational readiness. Israir Airbus A320, Credit: Oyoyoy via Wikimedia Commons Israir Sees A $20–40 Million Revenue Opportunity Until now, Israir’s New York route has competed primarily for passengers whose destination is New York. American connections let it compete for people going beyond New York as well. Israir estimates that this expands its potential customer market by 20–25%, creating an opportunity for $20–40 million in additional annual revenue. The filing though describes this as the larger addressable market rather than a revenue growth forecast. A codeshare on American’s flight also gives it something to sell when its own flight isn’t operating or its seats are full. For American, the near-term benefit is carrying Israir passengers on flights it’s already operating beyond JFK. Once American returns to Tel Aviv, Israir can also help sell seats on that flight through its own customer base and distribution in Israel. El Al And Delta Already Have A More Complete Partnership American is playing catch-up in Israel. Delta restored daily JFK–Tel Aviv service in September, and United returned that month as well. El Al and Arkia also serve the New York market. United can combine its Tel Aviv flying with its Newark hub. El Al has a Delta relationship that includes reciprocal codeshares, mileage earning and redemption, and elite benefits. That partnership began in 2024. What Passengers Get—And What They Don’t The immediate customer proposition is an easier connecting itinerary once the agreement goes live. Israir operates out of American’s JFK Terminal 8, so passengers won’t need to change terminals (and terminals aren’t connected airside at JFK). Passengers arriving from Israel still need to clear U.S. immigration and customs. Checking a bag through to the final destination doesn’t eliminate collecting and rechecking it on arrival in the United States. American also confirms Greenwich Lounge access at JFK for passengers flying Israir business class. However, there are no AAdvantage mileage earning, Loyalty Points, award redemptions or reciprocal elite benefits on Israir. The airlines say they’ll consider broader codesharing and AAdvantage benefits later. Hopefully status-earning and award redemption on Israir comes to fruition in the future.     💡 Key Takeaways
    • Sources indicate that looking to buy Southwest points?
    • While there has long been value in strategically buying points, the concept of a revenue based frequent flyer program selling points can be tougher to rationalize.
    • Link: Buy Southwest Rapid Rewards points with this promotion for 50% off.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that looking to buy Southwest points? Rapid Rewards is presently offering up to a 50% discount on purchased points, which is an opportunity to acquire them for just 1.5 cents each. Is that a good deal?

    While there has long been value in strategically buying points, the concept of a revenue based frequent flyer program selling points can be tougher to rationalize. So that I don’t bury the lede, let me say that I’d only buy points in a very narrow set of circumstances, like if trying to top off a points balance for a specific redemption.

    Link: Buy Southwest Rapid Rewards points with this promotion for 50% off.

    However, the best version of the offer to buy Southwest points provides up to a 50% discount, structured as follows:.

    Ordinarily you can buy Southwest points for 3.0 cents each, and that price is inclusive of the 7.5% federal excise tax. Given the limit of being able to purchase up to 100,000 Rapid Rewards points per day, that means if you maxed out this promotion, you could buy 100,000 points for $1,500, which is a cost of 1.5 cents per point.

    Southwest sells points in increments of 1,000 points, with 2,000 points being the minimum. Ordinarily there’s a daily maximum of buying 60,000 points, but during this promotion, that cap has been increased to 100,000 points.

    Just in the interest of being thorough, some Rapid Rewards members may be eligible for smaller percentage discounts, so let me crunch the numbers on those potential offers:.

    Southwest has no annual limit on how many Rapid Rewards points you can buy. The only restriction is that you can ordinarily buy at most 60,000 points per calendar day. During this promotion, that cap has been increased to 100,000 points, though.

    In a recent development, note that the purchase of Southwest points is non-refundable, and buying Southwest points doesn’t count toward Rapid Rewards elite status or Companion Pass qualification. Purchased points typically post nearly instantly, but in some cases, it can take up to 72 hours for them to post.

    Sources indicate that southwest Rapid Rewards frequently offers promotions on purchasing points. When the program does have a buy points promotion, the 50% discount offer is pretty standard. So I’d recommend buying points based on when you have a relatively immediate use for redeeming them, rather than anything else.

    Below is a chart with some of the recent Southwest buy points promotions that we’ve seen, before this one.

    If you’d like to buy Southwest Airlines points, note that purchases are processed by points.com, meaning they don’t count as an airfare purchase for the purposes of credit card spending. Therefore this wouldn’t be treated as a Southwest purchase if you’re using a Rapid Rewards credit card.

    It has been revealed that I’d recommend using a card on which you’re trying to reach a minimum spending requirement, or otherwise, a credit card that maximizes your return on everyday spending. See this post for more on which credit cards are best for buying points.

    Southwest Rapid Rewards is a revenue based frequent flyer program, and the number of points required for a flight is roughly correlated to the revenue cost of a flight. However, there is a dynamic element to the pricing, whereby the value you get per point varies significantly, based on the flight and fare class you redeem for. With this, we’re seeing redemption values as low as 1.1 cents per point, and as high as 1.5 cents per point, give or take.

    As you can tell, there are probably few situations where it makes sense to buy points for 1.5 cents (or more) each, when they can’t be redeemed for that, best case scenario.

    Industry observers note that let me cut to the chase — there are few situations where it makes sense to purchase Rapid Rewards points. Even at the discounted cost, there’s not usually value in buying points for 1.5 cents each when you can typically only redeem them for less than that. So don’t buy these points speculatively, unless you know exactly what you’re doing, and have a redemption in mind.

    There are three potential scenarios I’d like to address, including the main scenario where I think it could make sense (but not really), which is to build up a balance of Southwest points, given the flexibility this provides.

    Some might buy Rapid Rewards points in order to top off their account so they have enough points for a Rapid Rewards award ticket. I guess this might be worth it to some if you need a small number of points, though personally I’d just keep collecting points and then redeem with your next ticket.

    The Southwest Airlines Companion Pass is one of the best values in domestic travel. If you qualify for this, you can always have a companion travel with you for just the standard taxes, regardless of whether you’re booking a cash ticket or redeeming points.

    For those with a Companion Pass, buying Southwest points could get you outsized value:.

    According to recent reports, however, there’s still absolutely zero reason to do that. You’d be better off just booking a paid ticket and then having a companion fly with you.

    Recent findings suggest that there is one major benefit in general to paying for a ticket with Southwest Rapid Rewards points rather than cash. While Southwest Airlines has no change fees on both revenue and award tickets on most kinds of fares:.

    I do think there’s significant value in having a stash of Rapid Rewards points. I use this when I speculatively want to book travel (including for friends and family), since there’s no downside.

    If you’re looking to earn Southwest points, there are plenty of ways to rack up this currency with credit card rewards:.

    On top of that, Rapid Rewards has a variety of co-branded Chase credit cards, which can be a great way to rack up rewards. This includes cards like the Southwest Rapid Rewards® Priority Credit Card (learn more), Southwest® Rapid Rewards® Performance Business Credit Card (learn more), etc.

    It has been revealed that through December 31, 2026, Southwest is selling Rapid Rewards points with a discount of up to 50%, which brings the cost down to as little as 1.5 cents per point. I still don’t think there are many circumstances under which it makes sense to buy points, given that Rapid Rewards is a revenue based frequent flyer program, and points can typically only be redeemed for 1.1-1.5 cents each toward the cost of a ticket.

    American Airlines Says Operations Chief David Seymour Will Retire — With Dismissal-Style Severance

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 24 min read (4814 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • American Airlines chief operating officer David Seymour is leaving the job December 31.
    • In a recent development, [T]he Firm will provide Mr.
    • JonCarlo “JC” Gulbranson takes over January 1, reporting directly to Isom.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    American Airlines chief operating officer David Seymour is leaving the job December 31. CEO Robert Isom calls it a retirement. The agreement American signed with Seymour gives him severance on terms normally reserved for dismissal without cause or resignation for good reason. American’s last proxy put the cash severance alone at $2,750,625 for a hypothetical departure on December 31, 2025, with total value over $7 million. The airline hasn’t disclosed the final amount for this exit. [T]he Manufacturer will provide Mr. Seymour with the severance payments and benefits pursuant to the covered termination provisions set forth in his previously disclosed Severance Agreement with the Company dated as of September 20, 2023.

    In a recent development, [T]he Firm will provide Mr. Seymour with the severance payments and benefits pursuant to the covered termination provisions set forth in his previously disclosed Severance Agreement with the Company dated as of September 20, 2023.

    JonCarlo “JC” Gulbranson takes over January 1, reporting directly to Isom. He’s the executive I flagged as Seymour’s likely successor in August, when American handed him much of the job.

    In a recent development, aviation watchdog JonNYC shared Isom’s message to employees. Isom thanks Seymour for his friendship and his work bringing US Airways and American together. Before joining America West in 1999, Seymour led a platoon in the 82nd Airborne. Just last month he went back to West Point and Fort Bragg with Medal of Honor recipients to meet the cadets and soldiers who followed him there.

    AA pic.twitter.com/9919XVOKrW — JonNYC (@xJonNYC) November 20, 2026.

    Under Seymour’s contract, cash severance is 18 months of salary plus a year and a half of target bonus. He also gets money for 18 months of health premiums, and his stock can keep vesting during those 18 months. Between cash, stock, health premiums and flight benefits he’d already earned, American’s illustration in its latest proxy came to $7.13 million. Separately, Seymour remains eligible for his 2026 annual bonus. His advisory job pays $25,000 a month for up to three months ($75,000), plus executive benefits. His contract calculates severance using pay immediately before termination. Seymour has to sign a release and honor his existing restrictions, and American says it’ll file the full transition letter with its annual report. Those flight benefits include lifetime confirmed personal travel in any cabin for Seymour and his immediate family, Admirals Club access and another 12 confirmed roundtrips a year for friends and other relatives. The Handoff Started In August When American put Heather Garboden in charge of the customer experience, they gave her two bosses. She was supposed to persuade customers to pay more to fly American while reporting both to commercial and to the executive responsible for getting flights off the gate on time. When a pilot asked Seymour in 2022 what American was doing about poor customer satisfaction, his answer was “I think we’re on a good path to get there.” He went on to talk about running the operation. What was Garboden supposed to do when the catering truck was late and the choice was a delayed departure or six hours in first class without meals? In August Garboden began reporting solely to chief commercial officer Nat Pieper and picked up catering, reservations and service recovery. Pieper also got marketing, brand, advertising and partnerships as American broke up Global Engagement head Ron DeFeo’s group. Caroline Clayton took corporate communications. Then I reported network chief Brian Znotins was leaving as Pieper set out to rebuild flying in big cities where American had pulled back. Seymour actually picked up American Eagle in August. But Gulbranson got the airports and operations planning on top of flight operations, flight attendants and the control center. Now he gets safety, regulatory compliance and aircraft maintenance, too. We don’t know who first proposed retirement, but this looks to me like a negotiated handoff that was already well underway. American Had To Retrofit Planes It Had Just Retrofitted While there are numerous stories like it – such as insufficient oversight of outsourced Maintenance, Repair, and Overhaul – I always think of a few things about Seymour’s tenure. One is explaining why the airline wouldn’t invest in RFID baggage tags like Delta despite perpetually bottom of the industry performance in mishandled bags. Another is failing to fix ‘Concept D’ business class seats that rocked. And the biggest is mismanaging cabin retrofits of the domestic fleet. Seymour was running integrated operations when the first American Airlines 737 MAX introduced the cabin that would go into its existing 737s and Airbus A321s. A flight attendant eventually asked whether anyone had built a mockup before committing to it. They hadn’t. Doug Parker stated network planning had largely driven the design. Seymour called it “a mistake that should not have happened” and later explained what American had changed. For subsequent cabins they’d bring in real seats, build overhead bins and try pushing a service cart through. In his words, “We do mockups and not just you know ‘tape it out.’” Flight attendants working in the back galley had to help passengers get out of the lavatories because the two doors opened into each other and caught. The sinks were too shallow for the water pressure. I washed my hands on the inaugural flight and got water all over my shirt and pants, as did everyone else. Up front, the seat supports took up the space where a first class passenger was supposed to put a bag. American was still installing the interior after deciding to fix it. Project Oasis put the newly introduced seats into existing 737s. Then Project Kodiak went back into planes they’d already redone to fix the storage, give the first row some legroom back and add the device holders coach passengers already had. How Well Did American Actually Run? After the troubled summer of 2019, American gave Seymour responsibility for all operations. The following June he got the chief operating officer title and added flight service. For years my frustration was that when the operation fell short, the answer seemed to be to give the executive running it a bigger job. In 2023 American completed its highest share of scheduled flights since the merger and edged out United on domestic on-time arrivals. And spreading the Dallas schedule from nine daily rushes to 13 smaller ones helped passengers this year. The hub chief reported half as many missed connections in the first 17 days. But by 2025 American ranked eighth of ten network airlines for on-time arrivals. And the Transportation Department’s new figures show that Delta and United both beat American every single month from January through September 2026. Counting domestic flights including regional partners, American came in at 73.30% on time, United at 76.20% and Delta at 78.31%. American canceled 46,059 flights, or 2.99% of its schedule, against 1.75% at United and 2.25% at Delta. Credit: American Airlines One clue to what management valued is in that same proxy. In August 2025 the board gave Seymour a retention stock award worth about $2 million at target. The entire award turns on avoiding cancellations American counts as controllable. A flight that runs three hours late still counts as a success on that measure. The award measures performance through June 2027, so it can still pay out after he’s gone. Gulbranson is well regarded inside American. He started at Northwest, joined US Airways in 2008 and helped integrate flight operations systems during the merger. He’s run both the control center that decides what to cancel and the customer care operation that hears from the people who get stranded. Credit: American Airlines Listen to the two men describe January’s Winter Storm Fern. Seymour said the technology worked as intended and that he hadn’t seen reports of flight attendants sleeping in airports even as his boss Isom acknowledged crew had slept on floors. Gulbranson went before the pilots’ union board and told them where management had misjudged the storm and overestimated how swiftly they could recover. The union’s account called his assessment “unvarnished.” That’s one reason I’m glad he’ll be running the operation the next time it snows in Dallas and up the East Coast.     The Week: The Three Amigos Summit

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (241 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nationalreview

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • • We swear, it wasn’t our redesigned website that brought down email and the airlines.
    • • In an unprecedented trilateral summit in China this week, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin sat down with President Donald Trump.
    • NR Editors includes members of the editorial staff of our magazine and website.

    • We swear, it wasn’t our redesigned website that brought down email and the airlines.

    • In an unprecedented trilateral summit in China this week, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin sat down with President Donald Trump. Ahead of the summit, Trump set no metrics for observers to judge its success. The summit cannot be mentioned to have failed: It was not designed to achieve anything, and it didn’t. Of course, the president reportedly went into the diplomatic event of the year with some goals in mind. He reportedly sought commitments to nuclear disarmament from his Russian and Chinese counterparts, neither of whom had an incentive to agree to such limits. If Trump persuaded them to assist America’s efforts to isolate Iran economically, he has kept it a closely guarded secret. Putin sought to make the summit all about his war on Ukraine, but the Russian autocrat secured no meaningful promises on that front from Washington or Beijing. Only China, it seems, got what it wanted from the summit, which took place on its soil. The event allowed Xi to pretend to arbitrate the conflicts in which his great-power competitors are embroiled. The affair was not entirely unproductive, of course. It produced many joint statements of principle, which essentially state that all parties have agreed to keep talking.

    NR Editors includes members of the editorial staff of our magazine and website.

    On “The Week: The Three Amigos Summit”.

    Amex Centurion (black) card benefits — and how to get them without the card

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (175 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
  • The Centurion Card is an invitation-only product known for its high fees and exclusive perks, serving as a status symbol for cardholders.
  • Many of its benefits, such as hotel elite status, airport lounge access and concierge services, can be accessed through other, less costly cards.
  • Some Centurion-specific perks, like enhanced hotel credits, expanded lounge guest policies and unique event access, are harder to replicate elsewhere.
  • The card's value depends largely on how much you use its exclusive services compared to what you could obtain with alternative cards.
  • There is no published spending threshold or guaranteed path to receive a Centurion invitation, making eligibility unpredictable.
  • Centurion cardholders face significant initiation and ongoing fees, which far exceed those of most other premium cards.
  • Certain benefits, such as expanded Clear+ coverage, PS Salon visits and Centurion Lounge guest access, are uniquely enhanced for Centurion members.

    #77140. Britt bill would launch national office to combat financial fraud

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (497 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

    Britt bill would launch national office to combat financial fraud

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (497 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Britt has made fighting elder financial abuse a priority.
    • Industry observers note that A bill introduced by Sen.
    • The draft bill would establish a National Office for Scam and Fraud Prevention in the White House that would coordinate federal, state and private sector efforts.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Britt has made fighting elder financial abuse a priority. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    Industry observers note that A bill introduced by Sen. Katie Britt on Wednesday aims to combat a rising diversity of financial fraud by unifying the U.S. effort to fight it.

    The draft bill would establish a National Office for Scam and Fraud Prevention in the White House that would coordinate federal, state and private sector efforts. It is aimed at ensuring that federal agencies, law enforcement, financial institutions, telecommunications and technology companies and other groups work together, according to an overview from Britt.

    The newly introduced office would promote intelligence sharing across the public and private sectors, coordinate consumer education efforts and improve assistance for victims.

    Britt, R-Ala., mentioned the effort is needed because fraudsters operate nimbly utilizing social media while taking advantage of fragmented or disorganized responses from individual companies and government agencies.

    “This effort is about bringing everyone to the table and making sure our response keeps pace with the criminals who are exploiting new technologies and gaps between sectors,” she noted in a statement. “When we work together to identify threats earlier and share information more effectively, we can better protect American families and businesses.”.

    The office would develop a “lexicon of fraud” so that terms for different kinds of scams are standardized between various federal law enforcement agencies to promote a “whole-of-government response,” a Britt aide remarked.

    Sources indicate that the office also would work to broaden the approach to combating fraud beyond just having financial institutions reimburse victims. It would tap telecommunications and technology companies to address fraud at its source, such as rip-offs that start as text messages, social media posts or online advertisements.

    In a recent development, britt has made fighting elder financial abuse a priority. She is the sponsor of a bill that would allow state, local and tribal law enforcement agencies to use federal grant funding to investigate financial fraud, particularly scams targeted at the elderly.

    The measure highlights the prevalence of "pig butchering," a common technique where a predator cultivates a personal relationship with a victim over many months to extract the most cash.

    The House passed its version of the bill in September with overwhelming bipartisan support. The House sponsor is Rep. Zach Nunn, R-Iowa.

    Industry observers note that senior financial abuse also was the focus of a bill the House passed in an overwhelming 414-2 vote in June. The legislation, sponsored by Rep. Ann Wagner, R-Mo., would codify Securities and Exchange Commission guidance that permits mutual funds and their agents to postpone the sale of securities if there is a reasonable belief that financial exploitation of someone who is elderly or disabled is occurring.

    It's not clear whether the Senate will take action on these bills or Britt's by the end of the year.

    “If it doesn’t get through in the lame duck, it will continue to be a priority in the 120th [Congress],” the Britt aide noted.
