    Amex Blue Cash Preferred Review: A Top Cash Back Card For Everyday Purchases

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 14 min read (2706 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~14 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that if you spend a lot at supermarkets and want to earn cash back, the Blue Cash Preferred® Card from American Express is hard to beat.
    • In this post, I’ll cover the welcome offer, the bonus categories and how they work, the Disney streaming credit, and how this card compares to other options like the no annual fee Blue Cash Everyday® Card from American Express and the Citi Strata Premier® Card.
    • Link: Learn more about the Blue Cash Preferred® Card from American Express.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that if you spend a lot at supermarkets and want to earn cash back, the Blue Cash Preferred® Card from American Express is hard to beat. The card offers 6% cash back at U.S. supermarkets and on select streaming subscriptions, which can add up fast for families and anyone with a few monthly subscriptions.

    In this post, I’ll cover the welcome offer, the bonus categories and how they work, the Disney streaming credit, and how this card compares to other options like the no annual fee Blue Cash Everyday® Card from American Express and the Citi Strata Premier® Card.

    Link: Learn more about the Blue Cash Preferred® Card from American Express.

    Before I get into the Amex Blue Cash Preferred Card review, here’s a quick look at the most key features and fees:.

    And here are my thoughts on the main pros and cons of the Blue Cash Preferred Card:.

    When applying for a credit card, obviously the welcome offer, the eligibility, and the fees, are major considerations, given that they can be the first factors that impact interest in a card. So along those lines, let’s take a look at those details for the Amex Blue Cash Preferred.

    It has been revealed that the Amex Blue Cash Preferred is right now offering the following welcome bonus: You may be eligible for as high as $300 cash back after spending $3,000 in purchases on your upcoming Card in the first 6 months. Welcome offers vary and you may not be eligible for an offer. Cash back is received as Reward Dollars, redeemable for statement credit or for other select options. Terms Apply.

    That’s a solid bonus for a card at this price point, and the six month window gives you plenty of time to hit the spending requirement. Welcome offers vary and you may not be eligible for an offer.

    Amex cards tend to be fairly easy to get approved for if you have excellent credit. A few rules to know:.

    As you can see, this card is marketed as offering a bonus “as high as” a certain amount. The way this works, you can apply for the Amex Blue Cash Preferred Card, and then find out your offer amount. Then you can decide whether you want to accept the offer or not. That’s an unconventional approach for a welcome offer. At least Amex has the “apply with confidence” feature, so there won’t be a hard pull unless you accept the offer.

    Recent findings suggest that the Amex Blue Cash Preferred has a $0 intro annual fee for the first year, then $95. (Rates & Fees). That puts it in line with other mid-range cards. No first year annual fee is a nice perk, as it lets you test the card and see how much value you’re getting before you commit to the ongoing fee.

    If you decide the card isn’t working for you after the first year, you can always downgrade to the no annual fee Blue Cash Everyday Card.

    You can add authorized people to the card at no extra cost, so that their spending can help you rack up rewards.

    Industry observers note that I wouldn’t recommend using the Amex Blue Cash Preferred Card outside the U.S. or for purchases in foreign currencies. The 2.7% foreign transaction fee will eat into your rewards (Rates & Fees). There are plenty of other cards with no foreign transaction fees that are better suited for international spending.

    In a recent development, the Amex Blue Cash Preferred has some excellent bonus categories, especially if you spend a lot at U.S. supermarkets and on streaming. Below is a full breakdown.

    This is the headline feature of the Amex Blue Cash Preferred, and it’s the single best cash back rate for U.S. supermarket spending that I’m aware of. You earn 6% cash back at U.S. supermarkets on up to $6,000 per year in purchases (then 1%). This is the only bonus category with an earning cap.

    In a recent development, to put that in perspective, if you spend $500 a month on U.S. supermarket spending, you’d earn $360 per year in cash back from this category alone. That more than covers the $95 annual fee.

    In a recent development, note that supermarkets don’t include superstores, warehouse clubs (like Costco or Sam’s Club), or discount stores. If most of your grocery shopping happens at a traditional supermarket, this card is incredibly rewarding.

    It has been revealed that the Amex Blue Cash Preferred also offers 6% cash back on select U.S. streaming subscriptions. The list of qualifying services is quite long and includes most of the major platforms: Netflix, Hulu, Disney+, ESPN+, HBO Max, Spotify, Apple TV, Apple Music, Amazon Music Unlimited, YouTube Premium, YouTube TV, Peacock, Sling TV, and many more.

    If you’re spending $50 to $100 a month across streaming services (which many households are these days), that 6% adds up nicely.

    Industry observers note that the Amex Blue Cash Preferred offers 3% cash back on transit purchases, including taxis, ridesharing, parking, tolls, trains, and buses. If you commute by public transit or use rideshare services regularly, this is a solid bonus category.

    With the Amex Blue Cash Preferred, you also earn 3% cash back at eligible U.S. gas stations, with no caps. Note that this doesn’t include gas purchased at superstores, supermarkets, or warehouse clubs that sell fuel.

    For purchases that don’t fall into the bonus categories, you earn 1% cash back. This is the one weak spot of the card. At just 1% on non-bonused spending, you’ll want to pair this card with something that earns a better return on everyday purchases (more on that below).

    Recent findings suggest that with the Amex Blue Cash Preferred, you earn Reward Dollars that can be redeemed as statement credits, and there’s no minimum cash back balance required before you can redeem. It’s simple and straightforward, though it’s worth knowing that you can’t use cash back to pay your minimum payment due.

    In a recent development, as is the case for any credit card, it’s also key to consider the benefits and credits offered, if any. The Amex Blue Cash Preferred has a reasonable annual fee, so what are the benefits like? Well, they’re potentially pretty solid, and can help justify the annual fee….

    The Amex Blue Cash Preferred offers up to $10 back per month ($120 per year) as a statement credit when you use your enrolled card to purchase a subscription, including a bundle subscription, on DisneyPlus.com, Hulu.com, or Stream.ESPN.com U.S. websites, with no minimum purchase requirement. Subscription is subject to auto-renewal. (Enrollment required).

    Another Amex Blue Cash Preferred benefit is access to Amex Presale Tickets® and Amex Reserved Tickets®, which can come in handy if you’re trying to score tickets to an in-demand concert or sporting event.

    The Amex Blue Cash Preferred also includes an introductory 0% APR offer that can give you some breathing room on purchases and balance transfers.

    In a recent development, enjoy 0% intro APR on purchases and balance transfers for 12 months from the date of account opening. After that, your APR will be a variable APR of 19.74% - 28.74%.

    This could be helpful if you need to transfer an existing credit card balance and have some time to pay it off before interest kicks in, or if you need some extra time to pay off a big upcoming purchase. Just make sure you pay off your balance in full before the intro period ends, or you’ll be on the hook for interest after all.

    In a recent development, one benefit that doesn’t get enough attention is the Amex Offers program. This gives you access to targeted deals with a variety of retailers, just by registering your card and making an eligible purchase.

    Different Amex cards get different offers, so having multiple Amex cards in your wallet means more chances to save. Across my Amex cards, this program saves me hundreds of dollars per year.

    Sources indicate that the Amex Blue Cash Preferred Card has fewer travel protections than more premium Amex cards, but it does come with coverage to protect your rental car when you charge the rental to this card. The coverage applies for eligible damage or theft, and it’s secondary, so it kicks in after your own car insurance. There are some exclusions, and it doesn’t include liability coverage, so check your card benefits guide for the full details.

    It has been revealed that car rental loss and damage insurance: Eligibility and Benefit level varies by Card. Terms, Conditions, and Limitations Apply. Please visit americanexpress.com/benefitsguide for more details. Underwritten by AMEX Assurance Company. Car Rental Loss or Damage Coverage is offered through American Express Travel Related Services Company, Inc.

    The Amex Blue Cash Preferred Card offers the following benefits when you shop with the card:.

    It has been revealed that these are all helpful benefits that you hopefully won’t have to use (though they do provide some peace of mind). Just remember you need to purchase the relevant items with your card to get this coverage.

    According to recent reports, purchase Protection is an embedded benefit of your Card Membership and requires no enrollment. It can help protect Covered Purchases made on your Eligible Card when they’re accidentally damaged, stolen, or lost, for up to 90 days from the Covered Purchase date. The coverage is limited to up to $10,000 per occurrence, up to $50,000 per Card Member account per calendar year. Coverage Limits Apply. Eligibility and Benefit level varies by Card. Terms, Conditions, and Limitations Apply. Please visit americanexpress.com/benefitsguide for more details. Underwritten by AMEX Assurance Tech giant. When an American Express® Card Member charges a Covered Purchase to an Eligible Card, Extended Warranty§ can provide up to one extra year added to the Original Manufacturer’s Warranty. Applies to warranties of five (5) years or less. Coverage is up to the actual amount charged to your Card for the item up to a maximum of $10,000; not to exceed $50,000 per Card Member account per calendar year. Eligibility and Benefit level varies by Card. Terms, Conditions, and Limitations Apply. Please visit americanexpress.com/benefitsguide for more details. Underwritten by AMEX Assurance Company.

    I tend to lean toward points-earning cards for my own spending, but I totally get why a lot of people prefer cash back. It’s simple, flexible, and you can spend it however you want, including on travel. For that crowd, the Blue Cash Preferred is one of the best options out there.

    If you’re someone who is looking to earn cash back and spends a lot at supermarkets, then the Amex Blue Cash Preferred Card is an exceptional choice, in my opinion — 6% cash back will add up quickly.

    The 6% cash back on streaming, and 3% cash back on transit and gas stations, will add up quickly as well, and up to $120 Disney streaming credit could be worth more than the annual fee.

    However, this isn’t the card I would be using for your everyday spending, as you’d only earn 1% cash back in the categories that aren’t eligible for bonuses. So I’d acquire this card specifically with the intent of using it in the categories offering bonuses.

    So, let’s take a look at what other cards you should potentially be considering.

    If you like the idea of an Amex cash back card but aren’t sure about paying an annual fee, the Blue Cash Everyday Card from American Express (learn more) is the no annual fee alternative where you can earn as high as $200 cash back after spending $2,000 in purchases on your new Card in the first six months. Welcome offers vary and you may not be eligible for an offer. Cash back is received as Reward Dollars, redeemable for statement credit or for other select options. Terms Apply.

    Here’s how the two Blue Cash cards compare:.

    According to recent reports, in my opinion, the Blue Cash Preferred is well worth the annual fee if you spend a meaningful amount at supermarkets. The jump from 3% to 6% on U.S. supermarkets adds up fast. If you spend $500 a month at supermarkets, that extra 3% earns you $180 more per year, which nearly doubles the annual fee.

    The Blue Cash Everyday does have one unique advantage: 3% cash back on U.S. online retail purchases, which the Preferred doesn’t offer. If you do a lot of online shopping and less grocery shopping, the Everyday could actually come out ahead.

    The good news is that you can always start with the Blue Cash Preferred and downgrade to the Blue Cash Everyday after the first year if the math doesn’t work out.

    It has been revealed that if you’re just looking for the simplest cash back credit card, it’s tough to go wrong with the Citi Double Cash® Card (learn more). The card offers 1% cash back when you make a purchase, and 1% cash back when you pay for that purchase, for a total of 2% back on every purchase. That’s a solid return on everyday spending, and you don’t have to keep track of any bonus spending categories.

    According to recent reports, if you’re deciding between the Blue Cash Preferred and a mid-range card from another issuer, the $95 annual fee Citi Strata Premier Card (learn more) is worth considering. These two cards serve pretty different purposes, but they’re at the same price point:.

    The Blue Cash Preferred wins on supermarkets and streaming, hands down. If those are your biggest spending categories, the Blue Cash Preferred is the better card.

    The Strata Premier is the more well-rounded card overall. It earns 3x points across five major categories (dining, gas, supermarkets, airfare, hotels), has no foreign transaction fees, and its ThankYou points can be transferred to airline and hotel partners for potentially much more than face value. If you travel or eat out a lot, the Strata Premier likely comes out ahead.

    It has been revealed that one final card worth considering alongside the Blue Cash Preferred Card is the American Express® Gold Card (learn more). It has a significantly higher annual fee, but it’s unbeatable for earning rewards at U.S. supermarkets — you’ll earn transferable Membership Rewards points too, rather than cash back.

    Here’s a look at how they compare:.

    Industry observers note that the Blue Cash Preferred is the best cash back card for supermarket spending, and it’s not particularly close. If groceries and streaming are a substantial part of your monthly budget, this card can deliver serious returns, especially with the 6% rate on both categories plus the Disney streaming credit.

    It has been revealed that the annual fee pays for itself swiftly if you’re spending even a moderate amount at supermarkets. Pair it with a card like the Citi Double Cash for your non-bonused spending, and you’ve got a strong cash back setup.

    Just keep in mind that the 1% rate on everyday purchases means this card works best as a specialist, not your only card. Use it where it shines, and let a flat-rate card handle the rest.

    Recent findings suggest that denver airport’s top lawyer has spent eight months on paid leave, collecting a salary of roughly $225,000 a year. Now Denver wants a federal judge to let it fire him. But the airport’s general counsel Everett Martinez claims city officials retaliated against him for raising legal objections to their improper dealings and for refusing to help push out airport CEO Phil Washington. The city says he violated his professional obligations and wants to stop paying someone who can’t perform the job. Meanwhile, Denver has authorized up to $970,000 for outside lawyers handling his case and a separate employment lawsuit. The $470,000 budget for the first phase of his case is quite an expense for a fight between the city and its own airport lawyer. I’ve called Denver the worst airport in the country. It can work reasonably well as a connecting hub. Actually getting to and from Denver, through the terminal and out to a gate is another matter. This latest fight brings together several of the reasons the place inspires so little confidence: political interference, weak financial oversight, and executives spending their time fighting each other. The city’s November 10 filing argues keeping Martinez on leave is harming Denver during a budget crisis. Martinez wants paid leave to continue while he litigates, potentially for years. At approximately $225,000 annually, eight months works out to about $150,000 in salary, before benefits. That’s arithmetic, rather than a payroll accounting. The distinction between airport money and city money matters here. His salary is airport money. Martinez’s complaint says it comes entirely from the airport’s enterprise fund. That’s separate from Denver’s general fund. Airport revenue consists of things like airline rents and landing fees, parking and concession. That’s not money that can get moved to the city’s programs anyway. The outside defense contract is budgeted to city money. The council’s contract worksheet identifies the general fund as its funding source. So it’s actually the city that’s draining funds amidst a budget crisis, although it’s possible they try to bill it back to the airport. The $970,000 covers two cases. The city’s budget presentation allocates $470,000 to the first phase of Martinez’s case and $500,000 to a separate case. They’re authorizing spending ‘up to’ this amount at this stage. The amended agreement sets rates of $800 an hour for attorneys and $375 for paralegals. The firm is Wheeler Trigg O’Donnell, where city attorney Miko Brown previously worked. Funny that. Brown says a five-person panel considered four firms and unanimously selected this one, which Denver had used since 2011. She says she cast her vote for her former firm last. Martinez alleges he was punished after objecting to the Park Hill Golf Course land swap, warning against withholding information from federal aviation officials, and resisting pressure to help remove Washington. He also alleges discriminatory treatment and an ugly remark from Brown suggesting he get a noose. The city denies his allegations. The city didn’t want to lease airport space to a carrier involved in ICE deportation flights and Martinez wasn’t helpful in covering this up (it’s against the law). I coverde the Key Lime Air affair last year. Then I covered a memo supporting Martinez’s account that officials subsequently sought to manufacture a safety justification for the decision. The memo was written before his lawsuit, and another airport executive endorsed its accuracy. The Federal Aviation Administration opened a formal investigation into the lease denial with $90 million in federal grants at risk. Additionally, the city wanted airport property for a park. There are federal restrictions involved in transferrin ghte land. Martinez appears to have stood in the way (likely as he was obligated to). But the city has counterclaimed for breach of fiduciary duty, conversion and civil theft. Martinez may have a legitimate employment claim but that doesn’t give him the right to remain on the payroll throughout the litigation. He says his first amendment rights are being violated, but the Supreme Court generally doesn’t treat speech made pursuant to an employee’s official duties as protected citizen speech and giving the city legal advice was his job. And while he ostensibly also helped protect then-airport CEO Phil Washington, it’s not at all clear that Washington was doing a good job. (He retired August 1.) I covered Washington’s nomination to lead the Federal Aviation Administration and its collapse. He’d spent less than two years running an airport after a career in the military and public transit. During his confirmation hearing, he couldn’t answer a series of seven aviation questions from Senator Ted Budd. And his actual airport record is spotty. Construction oversight. A 2023 audit of the Great Hall project identified inadequate contractor oversight, procurement concerns and overcharges. The January 2025 follow-up found only two of ten recommendations for improvement fully implemented, and no corrective action on seven items. The construction debacle predated Washington, but I view his record as overall quite bad on accountability. Concession revenue. After an audit found weaknesses in rent collection and monitoring concessionaire deductions, the airport accepted 13 recommendations. By October 2025, only three were fully implemented. Accounting problems continued. Executive travel. I wrote about the extraordinary airfare bills for a Madrid conference. The ethics board’s written decision lists $12,047.01 for Washington’s airfare and $19,194.21 for his chief operating officer. My hunch is they were running for MileagePlus status. The board dismissed the ethics complaint for insufficient evidence of private gain, while sharply criticizing the spending and Washington’s response. His ‘need to be ready-to-work-on-arrival’ justification looked weak when he arrived three days before being on the program. The trains remain a good illustration of the airport’s deeper problem. I covered 131 breakdowns over a year. Most interruptions were brief. But passengers still lack a walking alternative to the B and C concourses. Denver is finally planning pedestrian routes through existing baggage tunnels, estimated at $300 million to $700 million, with completion expected in 2028 or 2029. That’s where I’d like to see the airport’s management attention go. Instead, airport users are paying a sidelined general counsel, city taxpayers are funding the defense against him, and the people responsible for running the place are arguing over whether their own lawyer can be trusted.     Concession revenue. After an audit found weaknesses in rent collection and monitoring concessionaire deductions, the airport accepted 13 recommendations. By October 2025, only three were fully implemented. Accounting problems continued.

    Executive travel. I wrote about the extraordinary airfare bills for a Madrid conference. The ethics board’s written decision lists $12,047.01 for Washington’s airfare and $19,194.21 for his chief operating officer. My hunch is they were running for MileagePlus status. The board dismissed the ethics complaint for insufficient evidence of private gain, while sharply criticizing the spending and Washington’s response. His ‘need to be ready-to-work-on-arrival’ justification looked weak when he arrived three days before being on the program.

    It has been revealed that the trains remain a good illustration of the airport’s deeper problem. I covered 131 breakdowns over a year. Most interruptions were brief. But passengers still lack a walking alternative to the B and C concourses.

    Denver is finally planning pedestrian routes through existing baggage tunnels, estimated at $300 million to $700 million, with completion expected in 2028 or 2029.

    According to recent reports, that’s where I’d like to see the airport’s management attention go. Instead, airport consumers are paying a sidelined general counsel, city taxpayers are funding the defense against him, and the people responsible for running the place are arguing over whether their own lawyer can be trusted.

The partnership is expected to expand in phases, delivering some benefits to customers. American plans to resume flights to Tel Aviv (TLV) as of late March 2027.

    How is this partnership expected to play out?

    For context, as of March 27, 2027, American aims to resume flights between Latest York and Tel Aviv, using the Boeing 777-200ER.     Recent findings suggest that the dynamics of this partnership are interesting. There are a few things to keep in mind:.

    When it comes to the new partnership between American and Israir, here’s what’s I find noteworthy:.

    All-in-all, this is a pretty casual partnership. Meanwhile Israir has a better framework for selling tickets beyond New York, which helps the carrier expand its potential customer base. But it is interesting how the codeshare is one-sided for now….

    In a recent development, american Airlines and Israir Airlines are launching a partnership for flights between the United States and Israel. Israir will be codesharing on American’s flight between New York and Tel Aviv (when that resumes in late March 2027, in theory), while American will have an interline agreement with Israir, allowing Israir passengers to connect on American flights beyond New York.

    It has been revealed that we may see a closer level of cooperation between the two airlines in the future, including possible AAdvantage perks, but nothing has been finalized there yet. I wouldn’t read too much into this partnership for now, and think it falls more in the category of “better than nothing,” rather than anything beyond that.

Then he declared, “I know a lot about air traffic control.” Watch Trump describe his pilot using another country’s air traffic control — Aaron Rupar (@atrupar), November 20, 2026 Air traffic control assigns clearances and separates aircraft sharing the same airspace. The controller responsible for your flight changes as you move between sectors and facilities. Your pilot can request a different route or altitude. They can reject an unsafe instruction. They can’t decide to use a different country’s air traffic control service because they like it better. And there’s a clear division of responsibilities. Pilots fly the aircraft and request changes to clearances when needed. Controllers coordinate the traffic. Could There Be A Real Story Behind This? I’ve tried to come up with something plausible, to create the most generous interpretation of these remarks. The best I can do is that Trump is confusing navigation equipment with air traffic control. Perhaps his pilot told him about a preferred navigation system, approach procedure or a piece of equipment he liked from overseas, and that became a story about choosing another country’s controllers. There are also real circumstances where an American flight uses foreign air traffic services: Crossing the North Atlantic. A flight to Scotland could pass through airspace handled by Nav Canada’s Gander operation and Britain’s Shanwick operation. Taking a route through Canada. A pilot could request a route that avoids congested U.S. sectors and spends more time in Canadian airspace (but it doesn’t give Canadian controllers responsibility for a landing in Tennessee). Flying in U.S. airspace assigned to Canadian controllers. “American airspace means American controllers” isn’t always true. Under a 1963 agreement, the United States delegates control of certain portions of its airspace within 50 nautical miles of the Canadian border. But the government assigned that responsibility, the pilot doesn’t choose their preferred controller. None of this would reconcile his comments with what he claimed on May 8, 2025. So, if I’m landing in New York or Florida or Tennessee, they’re using a system from another country. He repeated the story on June 27, 2025, too. So this is a recurring explanation of how he thinks flying works. The U.S. System Really Does Need Fixing I’ve been writing about the FAA’s antiquated technology and failed modernization efforts for years. Last week’s nationwide ground stop followed a contractor’s router installation that disrupted communications and radar information across much of the country. I’ve also pushed back when Trump claimed credit for the 2017 aviation safety record, when he blamed diversity hiring after the Washington crash without evidence, and when he suggested departing air traffic controllers could be quickly replaced. Training qualified controllers takes years. In fact, I supported the direction of Trump’s 2017 air traffic control proposal. He wanted to move operations into a separate nonprofit, with the FAA retaining safety regulation. A Canadian-style organization could finance upgrades without depending on annual congressional appropriations, and the FAA would stop regulating its own service. This year I challenged FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford’s attempt to rewrite that history as though airlines had hijacked Trump’s modernization plan and turned it into a debate over spinning off the system. Trump had announced the separate nonprofit himself. Maybe he think it actually existed, before he was President.     #77134. Industry News: Democrats nominate Jeffries to be House speaker, a historic first

    📅 18 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (910 w)

    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rollcall ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Democrats nominate Jeffries to be House speaker, a historic first

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (910 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that house Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., flanked by House Minority Whip Katherine M.
    • House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries won a closed-door vote of the Democratic caucus Wednesday setting him up to be the nation’s first Black speaker of the House, a historic step that follows Democrats’ staggering election wins earlier this month.
    • Jeffries, who had called for a recorded vote of the more than 250-member caucus that will serve in the next Congress despite facing no revealed opponent, won decisively, 251-11.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that house Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., flanked by House Minority Whip Katherine M. Clark, D-Mass., and House Democratic Caucus Chair Pete Aguilar, D-Calif., hold a press conference in the Capitol after the House Democratic leadership elections on Wednesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries won a closed-door vote of the Democratic caucus Wednesday setting him up to be the nation’s first Black speaker of the House, a historic step that follows Democrats’ staggering election wins earlier this month.

    Jeffries, who had called for a recorded vote of the more than 250-member caucus that will serve in the next Congress despite facing no revealed opponent, won decisively, 251-11. The margin suggests Jeffries will easily surpass the necessary 218 votes he will need on the House floor when the full chamber votes in January.

    “It's a high honor and a distinct privilege to stand before the American people today as a Democratic nominee to be the next Speaker of the United States House of Representatives,” Jeffries remarked at a press conference following the election.

    While Jeffries celebrates his win, he has continued to put an emphasis on unity before he faces what has been deemed the toughest job in Washington. Democrats’ massive majority will give him some margin for maneuvering as he balances the priorities of a complex caucus ranging from moderates to progressives.

    In a recent development, “Our job is to fight MAGA extremism, not each other,” Jeffries responded when asked about the 11 defections and what they mean for the next Congress. “Fight MAGA extremism, and to get big things done for the American people, and that is what we are going to accomplish together, beginning on January 3rd.”.

    Seven of the 11 members who intended to vote against Jeffries released a statement saying that conversations with leadership are still “ongoing” and that there is “work to be done,” but noting there has been “meaningful progress.” The seven included Reps.- elect Darializa Avilia Chavelier, D-N.Y., Adam Hamawy, D-N.J., Frederick Haynes, D-Texas, Melat Kiros, D-Colo., Donovan McKinney, D-Mich., Chris Rabb, D-Pa., and Claire Valdez, D-N.Y.

    “Whether on Medicare for All, stopping ICE terror, getting money out of politics, or ending the genocide in Gaza, our constituents sent us to Congress with a mandate on these concerns,” they wrote. “We have worked to secure commitments from Leader Jeffries in good-faith conversations.”.

    Newly elected House Democrats will meet with former President Barack Obama Wednesday night, where party unity will also be a likely topic.

    “This is the beginning of a new bargain, a new politics where hard work is honored and where people's voice is paramount, and where we have more confidence in the future than nostalgia for the past,” House Minority Whip Katherine M. Clark, D-Mass., said at the press conference.

    Rep. Nancy Pelosi, D-Calif., who made history two decades ago as the nation’s first female speaker, arrived for the vote chanting “Hakeem Jeffries!”, reflecting party leaders’ desire to start the long morning of balloting on a positive note.

    Jeffries' nomination followed the election of current Democratic Caucus Vice Chairman Ted Lieu, D-Calif., to serve as the caucus chair in the next Congress. Separate votes followed Wednesday morning, keeping Jeffries' leadership team intact: Clark, as the new majority leader and Democratic Caucus Chairman Pete Aguilar, D-Calif., as majority whip.

    At his news conference, Jeffries noted that Clark was also making history as the first woman ever to serve in the position. Aguilar will also be the first Latino to serve as majority whip.

    In a recent development, “We've been looking at people's talents, not a particular gender or race, and I think that's a good thing,” outgoing Rep. Steny H. Hoyer, D-Md., a former majority leader, told reporters ahead of the election.

    In a recent development, “I think Hakeem Jeffries is going to be a good speaker,” Hoyer continued. “He has the confidence of the caucus, and he has a good leadership team that is close knit and very organized.”.

    Jeffries expressed confidence in the weeks leading up to his securing the top Democratic spot in the House, brushing aside questions about incoming members who had mentioned they remained “undecided” ahead of the election.

    Industry observers note that pelosi was nominated for speaker by acclamation ahead of her first election to the position in 2007. But Jeffries’ allies portrayed his decision to move forward with a recorded vote as a show of strength after a group of incoming progressives had floated forcing a recorded vote in the internal leadership race.

    The entire leadership team will be tested despite their numerical advantage over Republicans by the same internal tensions facing Senate Democrats, where current Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer, D-N.Y., is being challenged for leadership of the majority by Sen. Chris Van Hollen, D-Md.

    Jeffries stated Tuesday that the approach to the caucus vote mirrored the caucus’ 2018 transition from minority to majority, giving members an opportunity to weigh in on who was best positioned to lead based on their “track record, experience and vision.”.

    Jeffries has already outlined some of his top priorities of his speakership such as a hefty healthcare agenda, immigration legislation, and a multitude of investigations into the Trump administration.

    He also signaled Wednesday another area where his party’s restive base is likely to close ranks: oversight.

    “House Democrats will hold the crooks accountable, not for partisan reasons, but for patriotic ones,” he noted at his news conference.

    LATAM Airlines unveils new A321XLR cabins with eye on US expansion

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (342 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The next frontier for the Airbus A321XLR is South America.
    • Sources indicate that after opening dozens of fresh transatlantic routes, the long-range narrow-body will make its debut with LATAM Airlines in March 2027.
    • LATAM, a close partner of Delta Air Lines, will outfit its fleet of XLRs with 174 seats.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The next frontier for the Airbus A321XLR is South America.

    Sources indicate that after opening dozens of fresh transatlantic routes, the long-range narrow-body will make its debut with LATAM Airlines in March 2027. The airline has yet to say which routes the XLRs will fly, but executives have previously outlined opportunities to connect the U.S. and South America.

    LATAM, a close partner of Delta Air Lines, will outfit its fleet of XLRs with 174 seats. Business class will feature 12 lie-flat suites supplied by Thompson Aero Seating in a 1-1 layout with privacy doors.

    The suites include 19-inch personal entertainment screens, Bluetooth connectivity and in-seat charging options.

    Recent findings suggest that economy features 13-inch screens at each of the 126 seats, which are supplied by Recaro, plus Bluetooth connectivity and USB-C outlets. The cabin includes 36 extra-legroom seats.

    “The Airbus A321XLR allows us to take our value proposition to the next level and elevate the travel experience for our passengers,” said Paulo Miranda, the chief customer officer of LATAM, in a statement. He described the interior, which features red, orange and blue hues, as “inspired by South America.”.

    LATAM executives have said it could fly the XLR on routes into the U.S. from its hub at Jorge Chavez International Airport (LIM) in Lima. However, those plans were called into question in May over the addition of a "connection fee" at LIM.

    According to recent reports, the airline and Delta serve six U.S. destinations from LIM: Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport (ATL), Los Angeles International Airport (LAX), Miami International Airport (MIA), John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK), Orlando International Airport (MCO) and, since January 2026, Salt Lake City International Airport (SLC).

    LATAM did not comment on specific route plans for the XLR.

    Recent findings suggest that the XLR is the second new airplane type for LATAM in as many years. The airline took delivery of its first Embraer E195-E2 in October. It will use the small jet to expand its feeder network in Brazil and support additional long-haul, intercontinental flying.

    Breaking: Grand Theft Auto VI and How We Spend Our Time

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (299 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Nationalreview

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Donald Trump just met with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping in China for a tripartite global summit — and nobody has any real news to report, except for Trump, so desperate for media attention that he’s giving interviews to anyone holding a hot mic and a video camera.
    • Every periodical you might care to read — even the political or news-based ones — has brought forward its big-think “review” of the game, now available on PlayStation and Xbox.
    • Industry observers note that jeffrey Blehar is a National Review staff writer living in Chicago.

    Donald Trump just met with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping in China for a tripartite global summit — and nobody has any real news to report, except for Trump, so desperate for media attention that he’s giving interviews to anyone holding a hot mic and a video camera. The lack of news is not just because of a (predictable) blackout enforced by the Chinese Communist Party, but because the collective consciousness of America has shut down for the next few days. If you thought the traditional four-day Thanksgiving Day Weekend was typically slow, get ready for a one-and-a-half-week productivity dip in the economy as the video game Grand Theft Auto VI goes live across the nation. Even National Review, as sober-minded as it is, has more than a few fans of the series on its staff.

    Every periodical you might care to read — even the political or news-based ones — has brought forward its big-think “review” of the game, now available on PlayStation and Xbox. For all I know we’ll be publishing one too. But I am not a gamer — not in the modern sense of the word, although I did whip out my copy of Battletoads for the NES the other day to prove that I’ve still “got it” — and this will not be a review of GTA VI. Instead, I want to talk about time spent — and time wasted.

    Industry observers note that jeffrey Blehar is a National Review staff writer living in Chicago. He is also the co-host of National Review’s Political Beats podcast, which explores the great music of the modern era with guests from the political world happy to find something non-political to talk about.

    On “Grand Theft Auto VI and How We Spend Our Time”.

    • Sources indicate that JSX has acquired Latest Pacific Airlines, and intends to bring the failed airline back with 42 seat Embraer regional jets.
    • I think this fits a company that’s been unusually creative about finding markets and figuring out how to serve them.
    • In a recent development, JSX is continually evaluating opportunities to support its long-term growth and bring its distinctive flying experience to more Customers and more communities.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sources indicate that JSX has acquired Latest Pacific Airlines, and intends to bring the failed airline back with 42 seat Embraer regional jets. That’s 12 more seats than JSX sells on its planes today, and it gives them a way to grow beyond the limits of their current operation. I think this fits a tech giant that’s been unusually creative about finding markets and figuring out how to serve them. They brought turboprops to Santa Monica’s shortened runway and used a free membership program to gain access to Teterboro in order to serve New York. JSX isn’t laying out the New Pacific strategy yet. Asked about the deal, they tell me: JSX is continually evaluating opportunities to support its long-term growth and bring its distinctive flying experience to more Customers and more communities. As part of that work, we are pursuing additional pathways that could provide even more ways to deliver our award-winning service in the future. Our focus remains on the exceptional experience, convenience, and hospitality our Customers have come to expect from JSX. New Pacific has filed its intent to resume flying and requested a waiver of the usual 45 day advance filing requirement. An operating projection calls for: Embraer ERJ145-LR aircraft with 42 seats. Two aircraft initially, growing to six by the fifth month. 10,106 flights and roughly 309,000 passenger boardings in the first year. Flights averaging about 1.2 hours gate to gate, with staffing growing to 104 employees. New Pacific used to be Northern Pacific, the startup that wanted to connect the mainland U.S. and Asia through Anchorage using Boeing 757s.     #77128. Dems express ‘points of anxiety’ over Trump’s summit with Putin and Xi

    Dems express ‘points of anxiety’ over Trump’s summit with Putin and Xi

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1216 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that president Donald Trump prepares to shake hands with Russian President Vladimir Putin as China's President Xi Jinping looks on before the welcome banquet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday, Nov.
    • Some Senate Democrats have heartburn about President Donald Trump’s planned Thursday meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping, but Republicans counter by saying he could get the Russian and Chinese leaders to budge on a list of challenges even as he appears politically weakened at home.
    • Recent findings suggest that trump arrived Wednesday in China’s Shenzhen economic zone on the banks of the Pearl River ahead of a high-level summit that was ostensibly slated to focus on paring each countries’ nuclear arsenal.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that president Donald Trump prepares to shake hands with Russian President Vladimir Putin as China's President Xi Jinping looks on before the welcome banquet at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, on Wednesday, Nov. 18, 2026. (Iori Sagisawa / POOL / AFP via Getty Images).

    Some Senate Democrats have heartburn about President Donald Trump’s planned Thursday meeting with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping, but Republicans counter by saying he could get the Russian and Chinese leaders to budge on a list of challenges even as he appears politically weakened at home.

    Recent findings suggest that trump arrived Wednesday in China’s Shenzhen economic zone on the banks of the Pearl River ahead of a high-level summit that was ostensibly slated to focus on paring each countries’ nuclear arsenal. But before he left, Trump signaled the three-way talks also likely would include the artificial intelligence race, Moscow’s bloody war with Ukraine, global trade and his standoff with Iran.

    According to recent reports, the U.S. commander in chief’s tendency to sound deferential to Putin and habit of referring to Xi as a personal “friend” concerns many congressional Democrats. But Trump’s GOP allies on Capitol Hill, despite this month’s midterm election losses, still describe him as a dealmaker who has a chance to use his final years to bend Putin and Xi toward U.S. interests.

    Rick Scott, a Florida Republican who sits on the Senate Armed Services and Foreign Relations committees, noted Tuesday he was hopeful that Trump could make some progress on at least one issue with the Russian and Chinese leaders.

    “As we all know, China and Russia want to destroy our way of life,” he remarked. “But it would be great to reduce … nuclear stockpiles and make sure we're not going to ever get attacked.

    Recent findings suggest that still, Scott sounded skeptical about two world leaders Trump has tried to keep close during his two terms. “But do I trust Xi or Putin? No, they're a bunch of liars.” Asked if he worries Trump might trust them too much, Scott replied: “I don't think he trusts him any more than I do. … I'm glad the president's trying. Hope springs eternal. But do I actually really believe something good's going to come out of it? I don't.”.

    Outgoing House Armed Services Vice Chair Rob Wittman, R-Va., noted part of Trump’s talks on Thursday “should be to make sure the world is a safer place, to make sure we don't have aggressive behavior like Russia in an unprovoked attack against Ukraine.

    “They ought to be talking about how they don't do those sorts of things, how they don't threaten their neighbors, how they don't try to intimidate through the assertion of force that they ought to be able to work together to make sure we assure a safe globe,” stated Wittman, who lost his reelection race earlier this month.

    That comment came one day after Trump told reporters as he left the White House for Asia that he sees Putin “backing down a little bit” in his conduct of the war with Ukraine.

    Sources indicate that “I think he could be tougher. I think he could be a lot tougher, frankly,” Trump remarked Monday. “I think he's backing down.”.

    Those kinds of deferential remarks about the Russian leader are a significant reason why some Democrats have heartburn about Thursday’s meeting.

    Senate Armed Services member Mazie K. Hirono, D-Hawaii, said Tuesday that she’s concerned about the Shenzhen summit because “I’m not sure what’s going to pop out of [Trump’s] mouth next — especially for a meeting with two guys he clearly likes.”.

    Sen. Tim Kaine, D-Va., also a member of the Armed Services and Foreign Relations committees, said he has “high hopes” for the trilateral meeting — but “maybe not high expectations.”.

    Sources indicate that “I have some points of anxiety. I'm nervous about any discussion about Ukraine that doesn't involve the Ukrainians. And, so, some of the advance to this is like, ‘We're going to talk about ending the Ukraine war.’ You can't do that without Ukraine at the table,” Kaine said. “So the desire to bring about more peace and stability, that's a good thing to talk about. But no conditions about Ukraine and ending that war without them at the table? Not so sure about that.”.

    During remarks Tuesday on the Senate floor, Minority Leader Charles E. Schumer criticized what he described as Trump’s misplaced priorities.

    “Enforcement of the new rules restricting China’s access to our most sensitive AI chips should start today,” the New York Democrat said, adding that Trump should focus more of his Asia swing on securing commitments from U.S. allies to block China from gaining an upper hand in the AI technology race.

    Trump touted just that on Tuesday during remarks in Manila at a U.S.-Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit in the Philippines.

    “Since I returned to office, we've made major trade deals with Malaysia, Cambodia, Indonesia, as well as Japan, South Korea, and almost everybody, frankly, at the table,” he remarked. “And we've made many other vital agreements across the region spanning energy, critical minerals and technology.”.

    But on Wednesday, Trump appeared to have pivoted to the trip’s main event.

    Industry observers note that he stood beside Xi at an Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen and smiled as Putin approached. Trump extended his hand and shook Putin’s as the Chinese leader looked on.

    Scott, a Trump ally in the Senate, said Tuesday he sees the president “trying to build relationships to try to make sure we don't end up at war [because] he doesn't like war.”.

    According to recent reports, trump signaled Monday that he might press Xi for details on an alleged Chinese spy who had an affair with Nvidia founder Jensen Huang, costing the AI mogul his job as the tech giant’s president and CEO. He also mentioned he could bring up Nvidia’s sales of sophisticated microchips that many lawmakers — Republican and Democrat — want to ensure remain in the U.S. for domestic AI development.

    Recent findings suggest that the administration’s response to the turmoil at Nvidia, with Trump even suggesting he'd support Huang returning as CEO, is a rare area where Republicans have expressed concern publicly. House Energy and Commerce Committee Chair Brett Guthrie, R-Kent., wrote to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on Wednesday seeking information about “the implementation of federal laws governing technology exports, in particular the application of export controls relating to semiconductor chips, the effect of which has a broad impact on America’s race with China to artificial intelligence (AI) dominance and the ability of U.S. companies to set global technology standards.”.

    Heather Williams, director of the Project on Nuclear Challenges at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, wrote this week that for the three leaders, the “path is fraught with challenges.”.

    According to recent reports, “Putin could diplomatically outmaneuver the Trump administration and make any progress on nuclear issues dependent on undermining Western support to Ukraine,” she wrote in an analysis for the Washington, D.C.-based think tank. “Even the optics of Trump and Putin negotiating while the war continues and as Russia ramps up missile strikes on Ukrainian civilian targets could be interpreted as undermining U.S. values.”.

    • A dozen cities in Los Angeles and Orange counties raised or updated lodging taxes in recent elections as cities prepare for a surge in visitors during the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.
    • Five months after Los Angeles voters rejected an increase to the city’s lodging tax, the surrounding suburbs hiked their own.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Photo Credit: Griffith Observatory with downtown Los Angeles in the background. Wikimedia Commons / The Fun Chronicles.

    A dozen cities in Los Angeles and Orange counties raised or updated lodging taxes in recent elections as cities prepare for a surge in visitors during the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

    Five months after Los Angeles voters rejected an increase to the city’s lodging tax, the surrounding suburbs hiked their own.

    Preliminary results show 12 cities in Los Angeles and Orange counties approving changes to lodging taxes on November 3, according to the California Local Government Finance Almanac. Ten created or raised rates, with two cities pushing their hotel rates above Los Angeles’ 14% tax. Two expanded their current tax to cover more types of stays.

    The changes come as Los Angeles and the surrounding area prepare for a surge in visitation for the 2028 Olympics, which are expected to draw in roughly 2 million visitors to the greater Los Angeles area, and as local lawmakers work to address widening budget gaps. Skift previously reported that lodging taxes can be an easy sell because the people paying them aren’t usually locals who vote.

    In most cities, the increases are "not a huge amount of money compared to other sorts.

    United Nigeria Airlines Flew Passengers To The Wrong City—3 Years Later, Chairman Admits They Lied About It

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2282 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Viewfromthewing

    ⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, united Nigeria Airlines flew passengers to the wrong city and blamed the weather.
    • Sources indicate that I covered this incident on November 28, 2023, including the conflict between the pilot reportedly acknowledging a wrong flight proposal and the airline insisting on a weather diversion.
    • Recent findings suggest that executive Chairman Obiora Okonkwo revisited the episode at the World Public Relations Forum in Abuja on November 17.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, united Nigeria Airlines flew passengers to the wrong city and blamed the weather. Three years later, they’re admitting it was all a lie. I covered this incident on November 28, 2023, including the conflict between the pilot reportedly acknowledging a wrong flight plan and the airline insisting on a weather diversion. Now, Live and Let’s Fly flags the airline chairman’s admission that the passengers’ explanation was right. Executive Chairman Obiora Okonkwo revisited the episode at the World Public Relations Forum in Abuja on November 17. A dispatcher had entered the wrong destination in the paperwork. The pilots flew there. The flight attendants apparently believed they’d reached the city everyone bought tickets to. He described the weather explanation as “just a lie” and offered this advice: “The best way of public relations is to tell the truth, but tell it responsibly.” Passengers Were Welcomed To Abuja While Sitting In Asaba On November 26, 2023, flight 0504 left Lagos with passengers booked to Abuja, Nigeria’s capital. It landed in Asaba instead, about 200 miles away. This was United Nigeria Airlines, not United Airlines. Passengers reported that the flight attendants welcomed everyone to Abuja but then everyone discovered where they actually were. November 26, 2023 — Peacock (@dawisu) Another passenger shared video: We legit got scared sha. Laff wan kee me 😅 pic.twitter.com/sWxbnJeDna— Lord Macky (@AugustineMacky) November 26, 2023 The airline’s original statement blamed “poor destination weather”, remarked the pilot knew about the diversion, and attributed the confusion to an incorrect cabin announcement. The plane eventually continued to Abuja. The Investigation Uncovered The Truth The flight used an Airbus A320 operated by Bulgaria’s Fly2Sky for United Nigeria Airlines. Fly2Sky said at the time that United Nigeria had assigned it a Lagos–Asaba flight the previous day and hadn’t requested a change during the pilots’ preflight briefing. The Nigerian regulator identified failures well beyond one person entering a destination incorrectly. In its findings there was: Poor coordination between United Nigeria’s operations center and the firm supplying the aircraft. No joint preflight briefing between the pilots and flight attendants. United Nigeria’s failure to monitor the leased aircraft through its operations center. Failure to follow the approved flight plan filed with air traffic control. The chairman story is about a dispatch error. The regulator, though, laid out several opportunities to prevent it. British Airways Has Done It, Too In March 2019, a British Airways flight scheduled from London City to Düsseldorf went to Edinburgh after the pilots received paperwork for the wrong destination. The passengers had bought a flight to Germany but the flight took them to Scotland. A few weeks later, Scandinavian Airlines sent a Copenhagen–Florence flight to Bologna. That was a deliberate decision made before departure because the pilots lacked the correct routing information for Florence. They flew to Bologna with prepares to bus passengers onward. It’s just that they kept this information to themselves. And in August 2025, I covered AirAsia X passengers being welcomed to Incheon after their Kuala Lumpur flight landed at Seoul’s Gimpo airport, about 20 miles away. Here’s the Instagram video from that coverage: View the video shared by @rizalhakimm_punyer on Instagram AirAsia X said it had intentionally diverted for fuel because bad weather had caused congestion at Incheon. It acknowledged an incorrect cabin announcement, said the captain corrected it, and offered travel vouchers. Okonkwo also used his conference appearance to discuss a passenger upset that an advertised 11:30 a.m. flight had left at 11:20. He said he’d initially wanted to shout back, but instead responded, “I apologise for United Nigeria Airline leaving on time.” An airline chairman giving a speech about accurately convey what on-time means. This was United Nigeria Airlines, not United Airlines. Passengers reported that the flight attendants welcomed everyone to Abuja but then everyone discovered where they actually were.

    November 26, 2023 — Peacock (@dawisu).

    Another passenger shared video:.

    Laff wan kee me 😅 pic.twitter.com/sWxbnJeDna— Lord Macky (@AugustineMacky) November 26, 2023.

    Recent findings suggest that the airline’s original statement blamed “poor destination weather”, said the pilot knew about the diversion, and attributed the confusion to an incorrect cabin announcement. The plane eventually continued to Abuja.

    The flight used an Airbus A320 operated by Bulgaria’s Fly2Sky for United Nigeria Airlines. Fly2Sky said at the time that United Nigeria had assigned it a Lagos–Asaba flight the previous day and hadn’t requested a change during the pilots’ preflight briefing. The Nigerian regulator identified failures well beyond one person entering a destination incorrectly. In its findings there was: Poor coordination between United Nigeria’s operations center and the manufacturer supplying the aircraft. No joint preflight briefing between the pilots and flight attendants. United Nigeria’s failure to monitor the leased aircraft through its operations center. Failure to follow the approved flight blueprint filed with air traffic control. The chairman story is about a dispatch error. The regulator, though, laid out several opportunities to prevent it. British Airways Has Done It, Too In March 2019, a British Airways flight scheduled from London City to Düsseldorf went to Edinburgh after the pilots received paperwork for the wrong destination. The passengers had bought a flight to Germany but the flight took them to Scotland. A few weeks later, Scandinavian Airlines sent a Copenhagen–Florence flight to Bologna. That was a deliberate decision made before departure because the pilots lacked the correct routing information for Florence. They flew to Bologna with plans to bus passengers onward. It’s just that they kept this information to themselves. It acknowledged an incorrect cabin announcement, said the captain corrected it, and offered travel vouchers. Okonkwo also used his conference appearance to discuss a passenger upset that an advertised 11:30 a.m. flight had left at 11:20. He said he’d initially wanted to shout back, but instead responded, “I apologise for United Nigeria Airline leaving on time.” An airline chairman giving a speech about accurately convey what on-time means.     FCC pick advanced by Senate Commerce after Democratic boycott

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (896 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Ted Cruz, R-Texas, talks with reporters after the Senate luncheons in the Capitol on Tuesday.
    • The fight over partisan balance on the Federal Communications Commission snarled a Senate markup Wednesday morning as Republicans advanced a controversial nomination despite a Democratic boycott in an attempt to deny a quorum.
    • Republicans on the Commerce Committee voted unanimously to advance the nomination of Danielle Thumann Severs, a senior counsel to FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, to be a member of the commission, alongside several transportation and communications bills.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Sen. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, talks with reporters after the Senate luncheons in the Capitol on Tuesday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    The fight over partisan balance on the Federal Communications Commission snarled a Senate markup Wednesday morning as Republicans advanced a controversial nomination despite a Democratic boycott in an attempt to deny a quorum.

    Republicans on the Commerce Committee voted unanimously to advance the nomination of Danielle Thumann Severs, a senior counsel to FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, to be a member of the commission, alongside several transportation and communications bills.

    The fate of the nominations and bills could ultimately be decided via a challenge on the Senate floor, according to a Democratic committee staffer, speaking on condition of anonymity.

    In a statement Wednesday morning, committee Democrats, led by ranking member  Maria Cantwell of Washington, remarked they objected to Thumann Severs’ nomination without a Democratic “pair” nomination and referenced a letter they sent to Chairman Ted Cruz, R-Texas, on Monday requesting the nomination be removed from the agenda.

    “Commissioner Anna Gomez could be re-nominated with all swiftness, as we have called for numerous times,” the group wrote. “This is not a problem we created, but a problem that the White House can solve.”.

    Recent findings suggest that thumann Severs, if confirmed, would give the FCC three Republican members and one Democrat, Gomez. The three Republicans could then constitute a quorum on the commission, allowing President Donald Trump to potentially fire Gomez. The commission generally has five members, three of the president’s party and two in the minority.

    Cruz said at the markup that there is nothing in the law that requires moving nominees in pairs, and that committee Republicans would continue their work on what he called a nomination that followed a “typical process.”.

    In a recent development, “Democrats will control the Senate, unfortunately, in January,” Cruz remarked. “But today is November 18th. The American people elected each of us to fulfill our duties, including advice and consent, for our full terms.”.

    Related: Threats to broadcasters hang over FCC nominee hearing.

    The Democratic staffer told reporters that because the committee did not adopt rules at the beginning of the 119th Congress, it has been operating under rules from the 118th, which required the attendance of at least one member of the minority party to constitute a quorum for reporting bills or nominations.

    “The remaining recourse is to basically go to the floor and . . . make an inquiry in terms of what took place today, and then there would have to be a formal ruling by the chair,” they said.

    They added that in determining whether the committee had a quorum to advance the nomination, “It would depend on how they view our committee rules from the 118th that we practice under for the 119th versus what the Senate rules are.” The staffer said they have not yet spoken with committee Democrats or Democratic leadership about plans for such an inquiry.

    Democrats also previously boycotted a committee markup in March over an aviation safety bill left off the committee’s agenda, after which action was deferred. The committee later came to agreement and rescheduled the markup.

    In their letter Monday, Democrats quoted Cruz from a 2014 statement about the nomination of Loretta Lynch to be attorney general.

    “As you wrote in 2014, controversial nominees ‘should not be confirmed in the lame duck session of Congress by senators who just lost their seats and are no longer accountable to the voters.’ We agree,” the letter stated.

    In a recent development, on Tuesday, Sen. Ben Ray Luján, D-N.M., wrote his own letter to Cruz calling for the removal of the nomination from the agenda based on grounds that Thumann Severs lied to the committee.

    Sources indicate that “While Ms. Thumann testified she did not work ‘on any media-related issues,’ documents obtained through Freedom of Information Act requests demonstrate that she worked on several media related issues, including on commitments that Skydance made to pave the way for FCC approval of its merger with Paramount,” Luján wrote.

    In a recent development, democrats have criticized the FCC and Carr for allowing media consolidation, including by Skydance. There has also been bipartisan criticism of Carr’s threats against broadcasters for speech he disagrees with.

    Luján told reporters Wednesday prior to the markup that he expects, under Democratic control next year, Carr and potentially Thumann Severs would be called to testify.

    “I have questions. I certainly hope that Brendan Carr will voluntarily show up to this committee when invited, and that other rules and tools do not need to be used,” Luján mentioned, responding to a question about possibly subpoenaing Carr. “But . . . everything should be on the table.”.

    Recent findings suggest that sen. Jerry Moran, R-Kan., stated at the markup that he spoke with Thumann Severs about her role at the FCC and her “lack of engagement” as the commission has made decisions regarding broadcasters. He also said he found her testimony at last week’s nomination hearing “comforting.”.

    “I have concerns with FCC action in regard to political speech, broadcasters, and she indicated in her answers . . . in a way that provided me with a level of comfort about her nomination in regard to that matter,” Moran mentioned.

    Moran also noted he hopes to meet with Thumann Severs before her nomination is brought to the floor.

    Industry observers note that riyadh’s hotels lost their peak season when the airport shut. With BA, Cathay Pacific and others suspended into the new year and Houthi strikes still hitting the capital, the recovery hasn’t started.

    It has been revealed that riyadh hotels had one of their worst months of the year in October. A temporary shutdown of the city’s main airport cut off inbound demand just as peak season started.

    Recent findings suggest that occupancy fell 34.7 percentage points year over year to 34.3% from 69%, according to CoStar’s STR. Only March had lower occupancy, at 28.3%. Average daily rate dropped 29.9% to $190 and revenue per available room (RevPAR) fell 65.1% to $65.

    “October and November are usually the peak season months for Riyadh, so the impact is much bigger,” said Kostas Nikolaidis, associate account director for Middle East and Africa at STR.

    The October demand collapse traces back to an attack on King Khalid International Airport. The airport closed after an attack on Oct. 10 that Saudi authorities said killed 13 people and injured more than 300. Some 86% of scheduled Riyadh departures were canceled between Oct. 8 and late October, according to Cirium data, Skift repor.

    Sanders: ‘Medicare for All’ will be HELP priority

    📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (664 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., holds a news conference in the Capitol on Nov.
    • Recent findings suggest that saying that “Medicare for All” is no longer “a radical idea,” Sen.
    • Democrats could bring it about through the filibuster-proof budget reconciliation process, the Vermont independent and avowed democratic socialist told reporters.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt., holds a news conference in the Capitol on Nov. 10. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call).

    Recent findings suggest that saying that “Medicare for All” is no longer “a radical idea,” Sen. Bernie Sanders mentioned Wednesday that he would prioritize passing the universal health care strategy if he assumes the chairmanship of the Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee next year as expected.

    Democrats could bring it about through the filibuster-proof budget reconciliation process, the Vermont independent and avowed democratic socialist told reporters. And the idea could be buoyed by an influx of progressive lawmakers elected in the midterms.

    Sanders noted Medicare for All is gaining support from voters across the country who are looking to overhaul the American health care system as costs have soared. Democrats on the committee will move the legislation “as aggressively as we can, as rapidly as we can,” he said.

    Recent findings suggest that his version, introduced in April and referred to the Senate Finance Committee, would implement the universal health care system over four years. In the first year, the the age of Medicare eligibility would drop to 55 from 65, while coverage would expand to include dental, hearing and vision care. The bill would also provide coverage for eligible children during the first year.

    The age of eligibility would fall another 10 years in each of the following years until the fourth year, when coverage would be extended to all Americans.

    Sources indicate that “If there has ever been a time in the modern history of our country . . . to address the crises facing working families, this is that time,” Sanders said, noting that Democrats will have a 56-44 majority when the 120th Congress begins in January, the largest margin for either party in 16 years.

    In a recent development, sen. Tammy Baldwin, D-Wis., along with nine other Senate Democrats, last week offered an alternative Medicare expansion strategy, which would lower the eligibility to those ages 50 and up.

    While who will be leading Senate Democrats is still an open question — Chris Van Hollen of Maryland is challenging Charles E. Schumer of New York, who has been the top Senate Democrat since 2017 — Sanders mentioned he is confident the Medicare for All bill will get to the Senate floor, “no matter who the [Senate majority] leader is.” Sanders previously expressed opposition to Schumer leading the conference.

    Asked about efforts to extend the Affordable Care Act enhanced subsidies, Sanders responded he’s “all in.” However, he added “the American people and elected officials understand the current health care system is broken.”.

    Subsidies that help enrollees pay for health care premiums on the ACA exchanges were expanded during the COVID-19 pandemic, but these enhanced credits expired at the end of last year, raising costs for many who relied on them to help defray costs.

    House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, nominated on Wednesday to be speaker next year, previously outlined broader health care priorities such as extending the ACA tax credits and reversing Medicaid cuts enacted in Republicans' reconciliation package last year. When asked Tuesday how far Democrats want to lower the Medicare eligibility age, Jeffries responded, “that’s all part of an ongoing conversation.”.

    Recent findings suggest that in addition to expanding Medicare coverage, Sanders reiterated his push to lower prescription drug prices. The Vermont lawmaker previously introduced legislation aimed at reducing the cost of brand name prescription drugs by linking domestic prices to international price benchmarks.

    To enact some of the agenda, Sanders may have to court Republicans.

    Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., mentioned last week that he intends to serve as the top Republican on the HELP committee next year. Sanders said Wednesday that his likely GOP counterpart “has shown an enormous amount of courage in taking on Republican leadership year after year.”.

    Sanders added that although Paul may have a different viewpoint from himself on committee issues, he looks forward to finding common ground.

    Recent findings suggest that senator John Cornyn recently blocked the nomination of the eminently qualified T. Elliot Gaiser to the federal district court in Texas, preferring a favorite-son candidate whom President Trump did not nominate. But the Constitution is clear: The nomination belongs to the president, not the distinguished senator. The constitutional power to “advise and consent” does not belong to a single senator, but to the Senate as a whole. Senator Cornyn’s use of a long-standing privilege conveyed by his colleagues usurps the power of both the president and the Senate.

    The “blue slip” privilege does not exist in the Constitution or even in the Senate Rules. It is a practice of the Judiciary Committee not to advance a judicial nominee to a vote without the approval of both of the State’s senators. Invented in 1916, its scope and application are entirely within the discretion of the Senate Judiciary chairman, Chuck Grassley. He ought to use his discretion to put Gaiser’s nomination to a vote.

    On the last day before the 2026 midterm elections, President Donald Trump gave a speech before the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool, a site of considerable scandal in his second term. He joked it should be renamed after him and spent considerable time discussing Washington, D.C. construction projects and resurrecting conspiracy theories about monument vandals. When the president did turn to the elections, more than 23 minutes into an hour-long speech, he seemed to foreshadow major Republican losses in the House and Senate, describing it as “The most key midterm, I believe, in our lifetime.”.

    The last day of polling indicates that Democrats have odds that are better than good to flip control of the House and Senate. The final results from the Latest York Times/Siena University polls report “The party is ahead in all seven states likeliest to decide control of the Senate: Michigan, Kansas, Texas, Maine, Ohio and, more narrowly, Alaska and Iowa.” The final predictions in the Cook Political Report included five additional shifts for Democrats in North Carolina, Florida, Tennessee and Virginia, projecting “that Democrats will win 15 to 25 seats, putting them at a 230- to 240-seat majority.” If a sweep happens in the toss up races, it’ll give Democrats their strongest majority since 2009.

    Meanwhile, early voting records have been smashed around the country, in places like South Carolina and Ohio. In Texas, more than 7.7 million voters did so early, surpassing the record turnout for a midterm election set in 2018. Across the nation, about 50 million ballots have already been cast so far, with the share of registered Democrats notably increased in several key state races. But according to the Latest York Times, around half the expected votes will come on Election Day itself, making it difficult at this point to determine how big a role early votes will play in the outcome.
